docs.title: NewBedwars
docs.text:
NewBedwars is a free Bedwars plugin for Paper 1.17 to 26.x. Arenas are built and configured in-game, the shop, scoreboards and boss bars are YAML files, and the same plugin runs on a single server or behind a Velocity proxy. PlaceholderAPI, WorldEdit and Citizens are supported but never required.

Download on Modrinth Get started Source on GitHub

Beta

NewBedwars is in beta, close to its first stable release. Gameplay is stable; please report problems on the issue tracker.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Gameplay

    Several arenas at once, each in its own world. Teams, generators, upgrades, traps and custom items such as golems, silverfish and bridge eggs. Rejoin, spectators, quick void and build protection.

  • Setup

    In-game setup with a checklist, or an automatic setup. Build from a schematic, copy arenas, and back up, restore, export and import them. Every game starts from a clean copy of the map.

  • Players

    Parties with clickable invites, arena groups with map voting, per-arena and team chat, isolated tab lists, stats and leaderboards. Six languages.

  • Customization

    YAML shop, upgrade menus, scoreboards and boss bars with placeholders. Game phases, dragons, generator speeds and upgrade prices are all configurable.

  • Networks

    JSON or MySQL/MariaDB storage, and a Velocity network mode with lobby and game servers. See Storage and Network mode.

  • Extensible

    An addon API with events and registries, update notifications, and the optional web panel.

docs.title: Arena setup
docs.text: Every arena lives in its own world. You build or paste the map, mark where the teams, beds, shops and generators are, save, and enable the arena. The full list of setup commands is in Commands.

docs.title: 1. Create the arena
docs.text:
/bw arena create myArena

This creates an empty world for the arena and puts you into setup mode in it. You start flying, so you don't fall into the void.

  • From a schematic: put your .schem file into the WorldEdit (or FastAsyncWorldEdit) schematics folder and run /bw arena create myArena -sche myMap. The map is pasted at the world origin. This needs WorldEdit or FAWE.
  • Later: /bw arena setup myArena brings you back into setup mode. /bw leave leaves it.

docs.title: 2. Choose a setup mode
docs.text:
A menu asks which setup mode you want; /bw setupMode opens it again. Each mode includes the commands of the modes before it.

Mode For Normal Placing everything by hand with commands: teams, beds, spawns, shops, generators, areas Advanced Normal, plus per-arena gamerules, shop and upgrade menus, generator levels, a resource pack, a game mode (/bw setMode), game phases (/bw setGamePhases) and a tab list layout (/bw setTablist) Automatic The plugin scans your built map and sets up what it finds (see below)

/bw setupHelp lists the commands of your current mode, and /bw info (or /bw info gui) shows what is still missing.

docs.title: 3. Set up the arena (normal mode)
docs.text:
Stand at the right place and run the command; most position commands use your location when you give no coordinates.

Waiting lobby

  • /bw setWaitingSpawn: where players wait before the game.
  • /bw setWaitingPos1 and /bw setWaitingPos2: two corners of the waiting area (it is removed when the game starts).

Teams (repeat for every team)

  • /bw createTeam <color> <name>, for example /bw createTeam RED Red. Colors: RED, BLUE, GREEN, YELLOW, AQUA, WHITE, PINK, GRAY, plus the other Minecraft color names (ORANGE, LIME, LIGHT_BLUE, CYAN, PURPLE, LIGHT_GRAY, ...).
  • /bw setTeamSpawn <team>: where the team spawns and respawns.
  • /bw setTeamBed <team>: stand on the team's bed (or give its coordinates).
  • /bw setTeamShop <team> VILLAGER and /bw setTeamUpgrades <team> VILLAGER: the item shop and the upgrades NPC (any mob type works).
  • /bw setGenerator BASIC <team>: the team's iron and gold generator.
  • /bw setTeamBasePos1 <team> and ...Pos2 <team>: corners of the team base (used for traps and the heal pool).
  • /bw setTeamBuildProtAreaPos1 <team> and ...Pos2 <team>: corners of the zone around the spawn where players can't place blocks.

Arena

  • /bw setGenerator DIAMOND and /bw setGenerator EMERALD: the island generators, one command per generator.
  • /bw setQuickVoidY: the height below which players die instantly. Set it a few blocks under the lowest part of the map.
  • /bw setMinPlayers <n>, /bw setMaxInTeam <n>, /bw setWaitingTime <seconds>: change the defaults from config.yml for this arena.

Made a mistake? /bw remove team <name> removes a team, and /bw remove team <name> spawn (or bed, shop, upgrades, ...) removes one point of it. /bw remove generator <index> removes a generator.

docs.title: Choose a game mode
docs.text: New arenas use the defaults from config.yml (Squads on new installs; modes are in modes.yml). For another mode, create the teams with the right size and, in advanced setup mode, run /bw setMode <Mode> (Solo, Doubles, Squads, Rush, Duels or your own). It copies the mode's generators, game phases, upgrade menu and team size into the arena in one step, and warns when the arena has a different number of teams than the mode is made for. See Game modes and phases.

docs.title: Team selection
docs.text:
With the arena gamerule TeamSelection (off by default; in advanced setup /bw gamerule TeamSelection true), players in the waiting lobby get a team selector item and can pick their team with the menu or with /bw team <team|random> (random clears the pick). Players who don't pick are placed automatically at the start of the game. Two more gamerules fine-tune it:

  • TeamSelectionBalanced (default true): a team can only be picked while it is one of the least picked teams, so the teams stay even.
  • TeamSelectionPartyLeader (default true): only the party leader picks, and the whole party goes to that team.

The game keeps waiting while fewer than two teams have players. The selector item (TeamSelector.Item in config.yml) and all options are described in Configuration.

docs.title: Automatic setup
docs.text:
Pick Automatic in the setup menu, build the arena, stand in the middle of it and run:

/bw startAutomaticSetup [radius]

The plugin scans the blocks around you (radius AutomaticSetup.DefaultRadius, at most AutomaticSetup.MaxRadius) and finds:

  • Beds: every bed color becomes a team (Red, Blue, LightBlue, ...) with its bed set.
  • Generator blocks: diamond and emerald blocks become island generators (touching blocks make one generator). The nearest iron or gold block near a bed becomes that team's generator.
  • Marker signs for everything else. Line 1 is the type, line 2 the team color (empty means the team of the nearest bed), and line 3 an optional mob type for shops (default VILLAGER):
Line 1 Sets [spawn] Team spawn (faces the middle of the map) [shop] Item shop [upgrades] Upgrades shop [gen] Team generator. With DIAMOND or EMERALD on line 2 it adds an island generator instead

The used signs are removed. The quick void height and each team's base and build protection areas are guessed from the map.

Anything still missing is shown in chat with clickable [Set here] and [Skip] buttons. /bw startAutomaticSetup next shows the current step again, skip skips it and cancel stops; what was already set stays. A new scan never overwrites what is already set.

docs.title: 4. Save and enable
docs.text:
/bw save
/bw leave
/bw arena enable myArena

/bw save saves the arena and stores the map as a clean template; after every game the arena is reset from it. Run /bw save again whenever you change the map.

/bw arena enable only works outside setup mode, so leave it with /bw leave first.

An arena can only be enabled when it has:

  • the waiting spawn and both waiting area corners;
  • at least two teams, each with a spawn, bed, shop, upgrades NPC, team generator, base area and build protection area;
  • at least one diamond or emerald generator;
  • the quick void height.

/bw arena list shows every arena and, for disabled ones, what is missing.

docs.title: More arenas
docs.text:
• Copy an arena: /bw arena copy myArena myArena2 copies the settings and the map, so one map can run several games at once.
  • Arena groups and map voting: /bw group create solo, then /bw group add solo myArena. Players can join a group (fullest free arena first), and at the end of a game they vote for the next map of the group. All arenas of a group need the same number of teams and team size.
  • Join NPCs: /bw npc create VILLAGER GROUP solo spawns an NPC in the lobby that joins the group when clicked. With Citizens, select an NPC and use /bw npc set GROUP solo.

docs.title: Backups and moving arenas
docs.text:
• Saving keeps backups of the previous versions (how many: Backups.Keep in config.yml). /bw arena backup <name> makes one now, /bw arena backups <name> lists them and /bw arena restore <name> [backupId] restores one.
  • Backups made with /bw arena backup end in -manual and are never deleted automatically (remove old ones by hand from data/backups/). /bw arena restore <name> without an id restores the newest of them, arena file and map together; with no manual backup it uses the newest automatic arena file and map.
  • /bw arena resetmap <name> puts the map back to its saved state.
  • /bw arena export <name> packs the arena and its map into a zip in data/exports. Copy the zip to another server's data/exports and run /bw arena import <file> there; the arena is loaded disabled.

docs.title: Balance simulator
docs.text:
The repository contains a small tool in tools/balance/ that was used to choose the generator speeds, game phases and upgrade prices of the built-in game modes (Solo, Doubles, Squads, Rush, Duels). You don't need it to run NewBedwars. It is for server owners and contributors who want to tune their own values or check a change before trying it with players.

AI-generated

The simulator scripts, the tuning run and the first version of the mode values were made by an AI assistant (Claude, from Anthropic), working on the NewBedwars source code with the maintainer. The tool reads the plugin's real files and copies the plugin's generator and phase logic. Its player-behaviour assumptions and target times, however, are educated guesses, not measurements. Treat the results as a starting point that still has to be checked in real games.

docs.title: Why it exists
docs.text: Generators, phases and prices interact. A faster team generator makes every shop item cheaper in practice. Pooled income in a 4-player team buys upgrades much sooner than a solo player can. A short mode like Duels never reaches the late game if the normal values are used. Before 2.8 the values were set by hand and used for every team size. The simulator made those effects visible. In the old values, for example, a squad maxed Protection at about minute 14 and still had more than 60 unspent diamonds when the beds broke.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
It is an economy model, not a game simulation: there is no combat, movement or map. For one team it answers "with these files, at what minute can the team afford iron armor, Sharpness, diamond armor…, and how many diamonds are left over?".

Each simulated game runs second by second:

  1. Phases follow your GamePhases list. As in the plugin, a phase's actions run when it starts, so island generators level up at the right time and beds break when they should.
  2. Generators behave like the plugin's. The team generator drops one weighted resource every SpawnDelay, with an amount from 1 to MaxAmount, and Forge raises its level. Island generators drop on whole seconds. The team gets a share of the island drops, and that share changes from game to game: sometimes the team holds the middle, sometimes it doesn't.
  3. Players collect their base and island drops from time to time and die now and then, which loses part of what they carry. They spend everything they collect following a shopping list (balanced, rusher or defender): swords and wool first, then Forge, armor, Sharpness, Protection and so on.
  4. The tool records milestones: when every player has a stone sword, iron armor or diamond armor; when Forge, Sharpness and Protection are bought; and when Protection is maxed.

sim.py runs 200 games per mode and compares the median milestone times with target ranges. tune.py starts from the current values and adjusts a few multipliers per mode until the milestones land inside the ranges:

  • team generator speed
  • island generator speed
  • upgrade prices
  • Forge prices
  • armor prices
  • phase length

It prefers price changes over changing island generators, so maps still feel the same. export.py writes the results as the plugin's resource files.

docs.title: Using it
docs.text:
You need Python 3 with numpy, matplotlib and PyYAML.

cd tools/balance
python3 -I sim.py --preset baseline   # the old (pre-2.8) values
python3 -I sim.py                     # the built-in modes
python3 -I sim.py --mode squads --policy defender --games 500
python3 -I tune.py                    # search new values (about 2 minutes)

Reports and charts are written to tools/balance/out/. The inputs you are most likely to edit:

File What to change modes.yaml Your players and maps: teams, players per team, island generators, how often players collect and die targets.yaml When you want things to happen in each mode (time ranges in seconds) presets/<mode>.yml The values themselves: generators, phases, item and upgrade prices

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
• Assumptions drive the results. If your players fight over the middle more or less than modes.yaml assumes, the right prices change too. Adjust the file and run it again.
  • The targets are design choices. The only public reference numbers found were older community guides for similar servers.
  • No combat value. A Sharpness level and a stack of wool count the same if they cost the same. Whether diamond armor at minute 10 is "too strong" is still your decision.
  • Only the economy is modelled. Traps, dragons, respawn times and bed defence are not simulated.

Use it to compare configurations and to catch outliers, then confirm in real games.

docs.text: Command Where Description /bw join [arena\|group] lobby Open the arena selector, join a specific arena, or join the fullest waiting arena of a group. On a network lobby server <server>:<arena> joins that server's arena /bw rejoin lobby Rejoin the game you disconnected from /bw spectate <arena> lobby Join a running arena as a spectator /bw team [team\|random] game (waiting) Open the team menu, pick a team (name, any case) or clear your pick with random. On a network lobby server: <arena> = that arena on every game server, <server>:<arena> = only that one; game servers can only list groups /bw group remove <group> <arena> newbedwars.bw.group.remove Remove an arena from a group /bw group list / info <group> newbedwars.bw.group.list / .info List groups / show a group and its problems /bw group setitem <group> <item> newbedwars.bw.group.setitem Change the vote menu icon /bw arena info newbedwars.bw.arena Lobby server of a network only: how to set arenas up on the game servers (/bw arena list shows all servers' arenas there) /bw npc set <action> [target] newbedwars.bw.npc Turn the Citizens NPC you selected (/npc select) into a join NPC /bw npc clear newbedwars.bw.npc Make the selected Citizens NPC a normal NPC again /bw npc info [id] newbedwars.bw.npc Show the action of the selected Citizens NPC, or of a simple NPC by id /bw npc list newbedwars.bw.npc List all join NPCs with their action and location /bw npc create <entityType> <action> [target] newbedwars.bw.npc Without Citizens: spawn a simple join NPC (e.g. a villager) where you stand /bw npc remove <id> newbedwars.bw.npc Remove a simple join NPC /bw reload newbedwars.bw.admin Save arenas, send everyone to the lobby and reload the configuration. Parties are disbanded. Refused while an arena map is being reset /bw update [check\|download] (2.7-beta) newbedwars.bw.update Look for a new NewBedwars version on Modrinth/GitHub; download saves it (checksum verified) to plugins/update/, installed on the next restart /bw game <start\|forcestart\|stop\|forcestop\|nextPhase> newbedwars.bw.managegame Manage the running game you are in or spectating (start, stop, skip a phase) /bw game broadcast <message> newbedwars.bw.managegame Send a highlighted message (& colours allowed) to everyone in your arena. Available from 2.7-beta

/bw join <group> joins the fullest waiting arena of a group, so players gather in one lobby. When a game in a grouped arena ends, everyone still there gets a vote item (MapVote.Item in config.yml, slot 1 by default) and votes for the next map among the group's other waiting arenas with room for everyone. When AfterGameWatchTime is up, everyone joins the waiting lobby of the map with the most votes (ties and no votes pick randomly; parties stay together). If no map is free, everyone goes to the lobby. Turn voting off for one arena with the gamerule MapVote.

Note

/bw update or /bw update check checks now; /bw update download downloads the new jar into plugins/update/ and the server installs it on the next restart. It only works in-game; the console gets an automatic line when a new version is found. Settings are under Updates in config.yml (see Configuration).

Join NPC actions: GROUP <group> joins the fullest free arena of a group, ARENA <arena> joins that arena, and SELECTOR [group] opens the arena selector. On a network lobby server all three send players to the game servers. A group is a /bw group name; otherwise it is an arena name pattern (solo_*) or a team size (4x1 = 4 teams of 1). Hologram lines and update speed are set under JoinNpc in config.yml.

docs.title: Automatic setup
docs.text:
Pick Automatic in the setup menu (or /bw arena create), build the arena, stand in the middle of it and run:

Command Description /bw startAutomaticSetup [radius] Scans the blocks around you (default AutomaticSetup.DefaultRadius, at most AutomaticSetup.MaxRadius) and sets up what it finds, then asks for the rest /bw startAutomaticSetup next Shows the current step again (after you changed something by hand) /bw startAutomaticSetup skip Skips the current step /bw startAutomaticSetup cancel Stops the scan or the step-by-step help; what was already set stays

What the scan finds:

  • Beds (the head half): every bed color becomes a team (Red, Blue, LightBlue, ...) with its bed set.
  • Generator blocks: diamond and emerald blocks become arena generators (touching blocks make one). The nearest iron or gold block within AutomaticSetup.GeneratorSearchRadius blocks of a bed becomes that team's generator.
  • Marker signs place the rest. Line 1 is the type, line 2 the team color (left empty = the team of the nearest bed), line 3 an optional mob type for shops (default VILLAGER):
Line 1 Sets [spawn] Team spawn (faces the middle of the map) [shop] Item shop [upgrades] Upgrades shop [gen] Team generator (wins over a found iron or gold block). With DIAMOND or EMERALD on line 2 it adds an arena generator instead

Used signs are removed. The lowest block of the scanned area minus 10 becomes the quick void Y, and the base area and block protection area of every team are guessed from its points (padding in AutomaticSetup). Guessed areas follow the team's points until you set them yourself.

Steps still missing are shown in chat with clickable [Set here] and [Skip] buttons that run the normal setup commands. Things that are already set are never overwritten by a new scan. When no step is left, the plugin says whether the arena can be enabled; save with /bw save.

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text: Parent permissions grant their children. Everything not marked true defaults to op.

docs.title: Admin
docs.text: Permission Default Description newbedwars.bw.admin op All admin commands (grants arena, setlobby, managegame, npc, group, update, update.notify) newbedwars.bw.arena op All /bw arena ... commands (grants the arena.* permissions) newbedwars.bw.arena.create / .delete / .enable / .disable / .setup / .list op The matching /bw arena <action>. Holding only one of these is enough: the player can use that action (and sees only the actions they may use in /bw help and tab completion). .setup also allows the setup-mode commands newbedwars.bw.arena.backup / .backups / .restore / .export / .import / .copy / .resetmap op The matching /bw arena <action>. .import is trusted like console access: an imported map can contain command blocks (they run when enable-command-block=true in server.properties) and datapacks. Grant it only to people you would give console access newbedwars.bw.setlobby op /bw setlobby newbedwars.bw.managegame op /bw game ... newbedwars.bw.npc op /bw npc ... newbedwars.bw.update op /bw update newbedwars.update.notify op One chat line on join when a new NewBedwars version is available newbedwars.network.bypass op Network GAME mode: stay on a game server without a join request (staff, setup) newbedwars.proxy.admin - Velocity: /nbwproxy (list the game servers and arenas the proxy knows, and whether a newer proxy version exists) newbedwars.panel.manage op /nbwpanel (web panel addon: status and panel accounts) newbedwars.bw.group op All /bw group ... commands (grants group.create / .delete / .add / .remove / .list / .info / .setitem; each one alone allows only that /bw group <sub>) newbedwars.bw.bypass op Bypass setup-mode restrictions (for example entering setup worlds) newbedwars.chat.color op Use & colour codes in arena and team chat messages (others have them stripped)

docs.title: Player
docs.text:
Permission Default Description newbedwars.bw.player true Bundle that grants all player permissions below newbedwars.bw.join true Join arenas newbedwars.bw.lobby true Go to the lobby newbedwars.bw.rejoin true Rejoin after a disconnect newbedwars.bw.spectate true Spectate arenas newbedwars.bw.lang true Change language newbedwars.bw.help true /bw help newbedwars.bw.stats true /bw stats newbedwars.bw.profile true /bw profile newbedwars.bw.leaderboard true /bw leaderboard newbedwars.party true All /party commands newbedwars.teamselect true Team selector item and /bw team (also part of newbedwars.bw.player)

All player permissions default to true, so everyone can use these commands until you deny a permission with a permissions plugin. Ops always bypass the checks. /lobby and /lang need the same permissions as /bw lobby and /bw lang.

To stop a group from picking teams, take newbedwars.teamselect away with a permissions plugin, for example with LuckPerms: lp group default permission set newbedwars.teamselect false. Those players get no selector item, /bw team is refused and they are always placed automatically. Operators always keep it.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
All main settings are in plugins/NewBedwars/config.yml. Every setting also has a short comment in the file itself. After a change, restart the server or run /bw reload (this stops running games).

When you update NewBedwars, new settings are added to your config.yml with their default values; your own values are kept.

Other files are explained elsewhere: game modes and phases (modes.yml) in Game modes and phases, shop items, menus, upgrade prices and generators in Shop and upgrades, storage in Storage, network mode in Network mode.

docs.title: General
docs.text:
Setting Default Meaning ServerName "&6&lExample&f&lServer.com" Shown on scoreboards and boss bars (placeholders /servername/ and /server_name/) DefaultLanguage en Language for new players and the console: en, pl, de, es, fr or ru. You can add your own language file to the language folder

Players change their own language with /bw lang.

docs.title: Arena defaults
docs.text:
Used for new arenas. Every arena can change them in setup mode.

Setting Default Meaning DefaultMinPlayers 4 Players needed to start the countdown DefaultMaxInTeam 4 Players per team DefaultWaitingTime 20 Seconds of countdown in the waiting lobby DefaultRespawnTime 5 Seconds a dead player waits before respawning DefaultTeamShopGui exampleShop Shop menu (GuiId of a file in data/guis/) DefaultTeamUpgradeGui exampleUpgrade Upgrade menu DefaultGeneratorConfig Squads Generator preset (ConfigurationId of a file in generators/), see game modes DefaultGamePhase Squads ID of a phase list from GamePhases in modes.yml, see game phases

New installs default to Squads. Existing servers keep their own values (DefaultGenerators and Default were the defaults before 2.8-beta and are deprecated, but still work), and arenas keep the generator preset and phase list saved in them.

docs.title: Default gamerules
docs.text:
DefaultGamerules applies to all arenas unless an arena overrides a rule with /bw gamerule <name> <true|false> (advanced setup mode).

Gamerule Default Meaning RandomTeams true Players are shuffled into teams; false fills the teams in join order AllowParties true Parties can join together and are kept in one team AllowSpectators true Players can spectate running games AllowTeamChat true Team chat (messages starting with !) AllowGlobalChat true Chat with everyone in the arena AllowPrivateChat true false blocks private messages (/msg, /tell, /w, /r and the EssentialsX variants) from and to players and spectators of a running game. Admins with newbedwars.bw.admin can still send them AllowTeamDamage false Team members can hurt each other MakeSwordsPermanent false Bought swords are kept after death MakeToolsPermanent true Pickaxe, axe and shears are kept after death; false = lost on respawn AllowMultipleGolems false A team can have more than one iron golem at a time SplitPartiesToStart true When all players would end up in one team (one big party), split the party so the game can start; false keeps waiting for more players MapVote true In a grouped arena, players vote for the next map at the end of the game (Map voting) TeamSelection false Players in the waiting lobby get an item and /bw team to pick their team; players who don't pick are placed automatically at the start (Team selector) TeamSelectionBalanced true A team can only be picked while it is one of the least picked teams (keeps teams even); false = any team with a free slot AllowSpectatingOtherTeams true true = players waiting to respawn (their bed is still alive) can watch every team with the spectator compass; false = only their own team. Eliminated players and /bw spectate spectators can always watch everyone TeamChatByDefault false true = normal chat goes to your team only and !message to everyone in the arena (the opposite of the default). Players without a team (waiting lobby, spectators) always chat with everyone TeamSelectionPartyLeader true With AllowParties: only the party leader picks and the whole party joins that team; false = every member picks on their own

docs.title: Gameplay
docs.text: Setting Default Meaning BasicSword WoodenSword Starting sword (an item ID from data/items.yml) FullArmor false Give every player a full set of team-coloured armor at the start RejoinTimeLimitEnabled true Players who disconnect can come back with /bw rejoin RejoinTime 5 Minutes a player has to rejoin BedLeaveConfirmEnabled true Leaving with the bed item asks for a confirmation: click once to start a countdown, again to cancel BedLeaveConfirmDelay 3 Seconds of that countdown StartCountdown.Title, .Chat, .Sound Enabled: true, LastSeconds: 0 The big title, the chat message and the sound during the countdown before the game starts. Enabled: false turns one off; LastSeconds: 3 shows it only during the last 3 seconds (0 = every second) AfterGameWatchTime 30 Seconds players can look around after the game before the arena resets TntParticlesEnabled true Red particles above players carrying TNT IronGolemLifetime 120 Seconds a bought iron golem stays alive

docs.title: Chat and tab list
docs.text:
Setting Default Meaning ArenaChatEnabled true false = players in arenas can't chat at all. The gamerules AllowTeamChat and AllowGlobalChat also apply. Start a message with ! to send it to your team only LobbyJoinMessages true false = no " joined/left the game" message for players outside arenas (the vanilla one is always hidden). The texts are PlayerJoinedServer / PlayerLeftServer in the language files; /player/, {player} and PlaceholderAPI placeholders work in them TablistIsolationEnabled true Every arena has its own tab list: players in an arena only see that arena's players, and lobby players don't see arena players

Players with newbedwars.chat.color can use & colour codes in arena and team chat.

docs.title: Custom tab list
docs.text:
The tab list (header, footer and how player names look) is customised per arena with the layouts in tablists.yml.

Setting Default Meaning Tablist.Enabled true false = the plugin never touches the tab list header, footer or player names (vanilla look). Independent of TablistIsolationEnabled DefaultTablist Default Layout used by arenas that have none of their own

tablists.yml has a Lobby section for players outside arenas (off by default, Enabled: false, like the MainLobby boss bar) and a Layouts section. A layout has up to three parts: Waiting (lobby and countdown), Playing and Spectator (the spectator's own entry). Each part can set Header and Footer (lists of lines) and PlayerFormat; keys that are missing fall back to the other parts (Spectator to Playing, Playing and Waiting to each other). The shipped Default layout shows team-coloured names: {teamColor}{player} while waiting and {teamColor}[{teamShort}] {player} during the game.

Use & colour codes. Placeholders: {player}, {teamColor}, {teamName}, {teamShort}, {arena}, {players}, {maxPlayers}, {minPlayers}, {phase}, {phaseTime}, {gameTime}, {kills}, {finalKills}, {bedsBroken}, {server} and {online}. PlaceholderAPI placeholders (%...%) work too when PlaceholderAPI is installed.

An arena uses, in this order: the layout set with /bw setTablist <layout>, the Tablist key of the mode applied with /bw setMode, then DefaultTablist. An unknown layout name falls back to Default with a console warning. The tab list refreshes every second and when players join or leave.

docs.title: Scoreboards and boss bars
docs.text:
bossBars.yml has one boss bar per situation. Each one cycles through its Texts, Colors, Styles and Effects every Time seconds and can be turned off with Enabled: false.

Boss bar Shown to Default WaitingBeforeStart Players in the waiting lobby of an arena On GameInProgress Players and spectators of a running game On GameEnding Everyone in the arena when the game ends On MainLobby Players in the server lobby (not in an arena). /players/ and /max_players/ count all enabled arenas Off (Enabled: false)

docs.title: Scoreboard placeholders
docs.text:
scoreboards.yml has three scoreboards: WaitingScoreboard (waiting lobby and countdown), InGameScoreboard and EndingScoreboard. Each has Enabled, Title, TitleEffect (NONE or RAINBOW) and a list of Lines. Placeholders are written between slashes (/players/); the curly form ({players}) works too, in scoreboards, boss bars, tab lists, join NPC holograms and messages, and capitals and underscores in the name don't matter ({max_players} = /maxplayers/):

Placeholder Meaning /datetime/, /date/ Current date and time, or only the date /map/ Arena name /players/, /maxplayers/, /minplayers/ Player count, maximum and minimum of the arena /status/ Arena status /servername/ Server name from config.yml /server/ Network mode: this server's id in the proxy (Network.ServerId); a line with it is left out on a single server /phase/, /phaseTime/ Next game phase and the time until it /gameTime/ Time since the game started /player/ Name of the player looking at the scoreboard /teams/ Repeats the line once per team, together with /bed/ (bed status icon) and /yourteam/ (marks the viewer's own team) /player.stats.kills/, /player.stats.final_kills/, /player.stats.beds_broken/ The player's kills, final kills and beds broken in this game

The sidebar shows at most 15 lines; with many teams, blank lines are dropped first. Placeholders of addons (registerPlaceholder) work here too; PlaceholderAPI placeholders (%...%) work in the lines too (not in the title).

docs.title: Boss bar placeholders
docs.text: Boss bar texts can use /server_name/, /arena_name/, /players/, /max_players/ and /phase/. In MainLobby (no arena) the arena name and phase are empty and the player counts cover all enabled arenas.

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text:
There are no permission settings in config.yml. Every player permission (join, lobby, rejoin, spectate, language, help, stats, profile, leaderboard, party) defaults to true, so without a permissions plugin everyone can use these commands. To take one away from some players or groups, deny it with a permissions plugin (LuckPerms or similar). Ops always bypass these checks.

Removed in 2.8-beta: RequireJoinPermission and RequireLobbyPermission. The join and lobby permissions are now always checked, like all other player permissions. Old config.yml files may still contain both keys; they are ignored.

All permissions: Commands and permissions.

docs.title: Game modes and phases
docs.text: Game modes (Solo, Doubles, Squads, Rush, Duels and your own) and the game phases live in their own file, modes.yml, and are described in Game modes and phases. Only DefaultGeneratorConfig and DefaultGamePhase (see Arena defaults) and the Ender Dragon settings stay in config.yml; the dragons are explained on the same page.

docs.title: Map voting
docs.text:
Arenas can be put into groups (/bw group). When a game in a grouped arena ends, everyone still there gets a vote item and votes for the next map among the group's other free arenas during AfterGameWatchTime. When the time is up, everyone joins the map with the most votes (a tie or no votes picks randomly). If no arena of the group is free, everyone goes to the lobby as usual. Turn it off per arena with the MapVote gamerule.

Setting Default Meaning MapVote.Item.Slot 1 Hotbar slot of the vote item. Slots 0, 4 and 8 hold spectator items, so they fall back to 2 MapVote.Item.Material PAPER Material of the vote item

docs.title: Team selector
docs.text:
With the gamerule TeamSelection (off by default) players in the waiting lobby get a team selector item (slot 0 by default, see the settings below) and can use /bw team. The menu shows one wool per team with the players who picked it, the players out of the maximum and the status; a "Random team" item clears the pick. After picking, the item turns into the wool of the team. Players who don't pick are placed automatically at the start of the game, as before (RandomTeams, parties).

Turn it on in advanced setup with /bw gamerule TeamSelection true. Two more gamerules fine-tune it:

Gamerule Default Meaning TeamSelection false Players pick their team in the waiting lobby TeamSelectionBalanced true A team can only be picked while it is one of the least picked teams, so the teams stay even; false = any team with a free slot TeamSelectionPartyLeader true Needs AllowParties. Only the party leader picks and the whole party (members in the arena) goes to that team; false = every member picks on their own and picked members are split from their party

If the picks would leave fewer than two teams with players (for example everyone picked the same team with TeamSelectionBalanced off), the game keeps waiting, or the countdown is cancelled, until someone switches. Players without the permission newbedwars.teamselect get no selector and are always placed automatically.

Setting Default Meaning TeamSelector.Item.Slot 0 Hotbar slot of the selector item (0-7; slot 8 is the leave item) TeamSelector.Item.Material WHITE_WOOL Material of the selector item. After picking, it turns into the wool of the picked team

docs.title: Maps and backups
docs.text:
The map of every arena is kept as a clean template in data/maps/<arena>/template. After each game the arena world is replaced by a fresh copy of it, so a crash or an accidental save can never damage the map. Edit the map in setup mode, then /bw save.

Setting Default Meaning Rollback.UseLegacySystem false true = use the old system (reload the world from the server folder, no templates) Rollback.AsyncCopy true Copy the template on a separate thread (recommended for big maps) Rollback.RestoreOnShutdown false Also restore maps when the server stops (slower stop). When false, a map that was in use is restored on the next start Rollback.UnloadRetryTicks 10 Ticks between attempts when an arena world can't be unloaded yet Rollback.TemplateExcludes session.lock, uid.dat, playerdata, stats, advancements Files and folders not copied into the template Backups.Keep 5 How many automatic backups of the arena file and map are kept per arena

Before a version update rewrites config.yml, a copy of the old one is kept once per version in data/backups/config/<version>/config.yml. These copies contain the MySQL password and the network secret as they were. If you change either of them (for example after a leak), delete the old folders in data/backups/config/ too.

docs.title: Automatic arena setup
docs.text:
Settings for /bw startAutomaticSetup (Arena setup).

Setting Default Meaning AutomaticSetup.DefaultRadius 150 Scan radius in blocks when none is given AutomaticSetup.MaxRadius 400 Largest radius allowed AutomaticSetup.GeneratorSearchRadius 20 How many blocks around a bed an iron or gold block counts as that team's generator AutomaticSetup.BasePadding 8 Blocks added around a team's points on the sides for its base area AutomaticSetup.BaseBelow 5 Blocks added below AutomaticSetup.BaseAbove 15 Blocks added above

docs.title: Join NPCs
docs.text:
Lobby NPCs that join a game when clicked. Make one with Citizens (/npc create, /npc select) and attach it with /bw npc set <GROUP|ARENA|SELECTOR> [target], or without Citizens with /bw npc create <entityType> <action> [target].

Setting Default Meaning JoinNpc.UpdateSeconds 2 How often the holograms above the NPCs update JoinNpc.LeftClick false Also react to a left click (right click always works) JoinNpc.Hologram.Offset 0.0 Move the hologram up (positive) or down (negative), e.g. -0.3 when the NPC name is hidden JoinNpc.Hologram.GROUP / ARENA / SELECTOR 3 lines each Hologram lines per action (empty list = no hologram)

Hologram placeholders: /group/, /arena/, /playing/, /waiting/, /arenas_free/, /players/, /max/, /status/.

docs.title: Storage
docs.text:
Where player data (language, quick buy) and stats are kept. Details and when to use MySQL: Storage.

Setting Default Meaning Storage.Type JSON JSON = files in data/ (one server). MYSQL = the database below; use it on every server of a network so stats are shared. On the first start with an empty database, the JSON data of this server is imported MySQL.Host / Port / Database / User / Password localhost / 3306 / newbedwars / root / empty Connection, also used by Network.MySQL. Uses the database driver that ships with the server MySQL.SslMode PREFERRED DISABLED, PREFERRED (encrypt when the server supports it), REQUIRED, VERIFY_CA or VERIFY_IDENTITY MySQL.AllowPublicKeyRetrieval false Only for MySQL 8 accounts with caching_sha2_password on a connection without SSL. Less secure

docs.title: Leaderboards
docs.text: Setting Default Meaning Leaderboards.RefreshSeconds 60 How often the leaderboard placeholders are refreshed, in seconds (at least 5)

docs.title: Updates
docs.text:
NewBedwars looks for new versions on Modrinth (GitHub as a fallback). Nothing about your server is sent.

Setting Default Meaning Updates.Check true false = never contact Modrinth or GitHub (also disables /bw update) Updates.Notify true Tell the console and admins (newbedwars.update.notify, one chat line on join) about a new version Updates.AutoDownload false Download new versions (checksum verified) into plugins/update/; installed on the next restart Updates.Channel BETA Versions to offer: RELEASE, BETA (releases and betas) or ALPHA (everything) Updates.CheckIntervalHours 12 Hours between checks

docs.title: Network mode
docs.text:
Only used with a Velocity proxy and the NewBedwars-Proxy plugin. The full guide is Network mode.

Setting Default Meaning Network.Mode NONE NONE = single server (nothing below is used). GAME = this server hosts arenas. LOBBY = no arenas here; joins send players to game servers Network.ServerId empty The name of this server in velocity.toml ([servers]) Network.LobbyServer empty GAME: lobby server to send players to. Empty = the proxy picks the least full lobby Network.LocalLobby false GAME: false = players waiting to be put into an arena wait invisibly at the world spawn. true = they are teleported to this server's /bw setLobby location Network.LobbyJoinMessages true LOBBY: show " joined/left the game" in the lobby Network.RestartAfterGames 0 GAME: restart the server after this many games, as soon as every arena is empty (0 = never). Your start script must start it again Network.TicketTimeoutSeconds 10 GAME: how long a player from the proxy waits for their arena before going back Network.StatePublishSeconds 5 GAME: how often the arena list is sent to the proxy while players are online Network.MySQL.Enabled false GAME: shared status table so the proxy sees game servers with no players online. Uses the MySQL connection Network.MySQL.HeartbeatSeconds 5 How often that table is updated

docs.title: Game modes and phases
docs.text:
A game mode bundles what an arena needs for one way of playing: the generator speeds, the game phases (what happens and when during a game), the upgrade menu and the team size. Five modes come with the plugin (Solo, Doubles, Squads, Rush and Duels) and you can make your own. In advanced setup mode, /bw setMode <Mode> copies a mode into an arena.

Modes and game phases are in plugins/NewBedwars/modes.yml. Edit it, then restart the server or run /bw reload (this stops running games).

docs.title: The modes.yml file
docs.text:
• Updating from an older version: the first time the new version starts, your GamePhases and Modes are moved from config.yml into modes.yml automatically. The old config.yml is backed up in data/backups/config/<version>/.
  • Built-in modes come back: built-in modes and phase lists that are missing from modes.yml are added to the file. Your own entries and comments are kept, and your own modes are not removed.
  • Invalid file: if modes.yml can not be read, the built-in modes are used and an error is written to the console. Fix the file and reload.
  • config.yml only keeps DefaultGeneratorConfig and DefaultGamePhase (the Arena defaults for new arenas).

Related pages: Balance simulator (tune phases and prices before trying them with players), Shop and upgrades (generator files, UpgradePrices, ItemPrices) and Arena setup.

docs.title: Built-in modes
docs.text:
Five modes come with the plugin. A mode is three parts that share its name; the files are copied to your server when they are missing (never overwritten, so your edits stay):

  • a generator file generators/<Mode>.yml (how fast generators drop resources, see Shop and upgrades),
  • a phase list with the same ID in GamePhases in modes.yml,
  • an upgrade menu data/guis/upgrade<Mode>.yml with its own UpgradePrices (see Shop and upgrades).
Mode Tuned for Longest game Solo 8 teams of 1 35 minutes Doubles 8 teams of 2 35 minutes Squads 4 teams of 4 35 minutes Rush 4 teams of 2 15 minutes Duels 2 teams of 1 12 minutes

The generator speeds and prices were tuned with the balance simulator in tools/balance/, so every mode has its own pacing.

To use a mode in an arena, create the arena as usual (team count and team size included) and, in advanced setup mode, run /bw setMode <Mode>. It copies the mode's generator preset, game phases, upgrade menu (and shop menu, if the mode has one) and team size into the arena and saves it. This happens once: arenas keep what was copied, so after you edit a mode, run /bw setMode <Mode> again in every arena that should get the change. If the mode refers to something that does not exist (a missing generator file, phase list or menu), nothing is changed and the missing names are listed. The single commands /bw setGeneratorLeveling, /bw setGamePhases and /bw setGui still work for fine-tuning one part afterwards. See Arena setup. The web panel can apply a mode to a waiting arena too.

docs.title: Modes in modes.yml
docs.text:
The Modes section of modes.yml lists the modes that /bw setMode knows (and offers in tab completion). A mode is a name with these optional keys; a missing key means that part of the arena is left as it is.

Key Meaning Generators Generator preset (ConfigurationId of a file in generators/) GamePhases ID of a phase list from GamePhases below ShopGui Shop menu (GuiId of a file in data/guis/) UpgradeGui Upgrade menu (GuiId of a file in data/guis/) MaxInTeam Players per team (a whole number above 0) Tablist Tab list layout (a layout name from tablists.yml, see configuration); copied to the arena like the other keys Teams Number of teams the mode is made for. It is not applied: /bw setMode only warns when the arena has a different number of teams 
Modes:
  Solo:
    Generators: Solo
    GamePhases: Solo
    UpgradeGui: upgradeSolo
    MaxInTeam: 1
    Teams: 8
  Trios:
    Generators: Rush
    GamePhases: Rush
    ShopGui: exampleShop
    UpgradeGui: upgradeRush
    MaxInTeam: 3
    Teams: 4

You can add your own modes by adding entries to Modes; they are kept when you update. An entry with the same name as a built-in mode replaces it completely (keys you leave out are not taken from the built-in one). Invalid numbers count as not set, and a mode that is not a section is skipped with a console warning.

docs.title: Phase times of the built-in modes
docs.text:
When each phase starts (minutes:seconds after the game begins):

Event Solo, Doubles, Squads Rush Duels Diamonds II 5:00 3:00 (with Emeralds II) 2:40 (with Emeralds II) Emeralds II 10:00 3:00 2:40 Diamonds III 15:00 6:00 (with Emeralds III) 5:20 (with Emeralds III) Emeralds III 20:00 6:00 5:20 Beds are destroyed 25:00 9:00 8:00 Ender Dragons 30:00 12:00 none Game ends 35:00 15:00 12:00

Solo, Doubles and Squads end as a draw; Rush and Duels end with the most kills winning.

docs.title: Game phases
docs.text:
A phase list (GamePhases in modes.yml) is what happens during a game. When a phase starts, it runs its Actions; Duration is how many seconds it lasts until the next phase starts. Arenas use the list named in DefaultGamePhase in config.yml, or the one set with /bw setGamePhases <id> in advanced setup. The built-in lists are the ones in the table under phase times; Default is the old list (about 35 minutes, deprecated).

GamePhases:
  - ID: Default
    Phases:
      - Name: "Starting phase"
        Duration: 300
        Actions: []
      - Name: "Diamonds II"
        Duration: 300
        Actions:
          - "DIAMOND_GENERATOR:2"
      - Name: "Bed destruction"
        Duration: 300
        Actions:
          - "BED_DESTRUCTION"
          - "DISABLE_REGENERATION"
      - Name: "Game end"
        Duration: 0
        Actions:
          - "GAME_END:DRAW"
Action Effect DIAMOND_GENERATOR:<level> Upgrade all diamond generators EMERALD_GENERATOR:<level> Upgrade all emerald generators BED_DESTRUCTION Destroy all remaining beds DISABLE_REGENERATION Turn off natural health regeneration DISABLE_TEAMS_FORGE Stop the team generators for the rest of the game (buying the Forge upgrade does not restart them) ENDER_DRAGON_START Spawn Ender Dragons (one per team with the Dragon Buff upgrade) ENDER_DRAGON_END Remove the Ender Dragons GAME_END:DRAW End the game as a draw GAME_END:MOST_KILLS End the game; the team with the most kills wins

Addons can add their own actions. Admins can skip to the next phase with /bw game nextPhase.

docs.title: Ender Dragons
docs.text:
Dragons are part of sudden death. Spawned by ENDER_DRAGON_START for every team with the Dragon Buff upgrade. Dragons patrol over the middle of the map, hunt enemy players (first those near a bed), dive at them and shoot fireballs. They never hurt their own team and disappear when their team is out.

The dragon settings stay in config.yml (not in modes.yml):

Setting Default Meaning DragonSpawnHeight 10 Blocks above the team spawn where dragons appear DragonIndestructibleBlocks OBSIDIAN, BEDROCK, BARRIER, END_PORTAL_FRAME, IRON_BARS Blocks dragons can't destroy (Bukkit material names). Beds are never destroyed. The map is restored after the game anyway Dragon.Speed 0.6 Flight speed in blocks per tick Dragon.TurnRate 6.0 How fast a dragon turns, in degrees per tick Dragon.PatrolHeight 15 Patrol height above the highest team spawn, bed or generator Dragon.PatrolRadius 0 Radius of the patrol circle around the map centre (0 = automatic) Dragon.Margin 10 How far outside the bases and generators a dragon may fly Dragon.TargetRange 128 Maximum distance at which a dragon picks a target Dragon.AttackRange 20 Horizontal distance at which a dragon starts a dive Dragon.FireballIntervalSeconds [20, 10] Seconds between fireballs for Dragon Buff level 1, 2, ... Dragon.FireballSpeed 1.0 Starting speed of the fireballs in blocks per tick

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Server: Paper 1.17 to 26.x (Spigot is untested)
  • Java: 16 or newer, or whatever your Paper version needs (1.18+ needs Java 17, 1.21+ needs Java 21)
  • No other plugins are required. These are optional:
Plugin Used for PlaceholderAPI Over 30 %newbedwars_*% placeholders (list) WorldEdit / FastAsyncWorldEdit Creating an arena from a .schem file Citizens Lobby join NPCs with a live hologram (without it, /bw npc create spawns a simple NPC)

For network mode you also need Velocity 4.x on Java 25 and the same NewBedwars version on every server. See Network mode.

Use a server (or a network backend) only for BedWars

Joining an arena clears the player's inventory, armor, XP, health and potion effects, and leaving puts them in survival mode. Nothing is saved or given back. Don't run NewBedwars on a server where players also keep survival or creative items, or put BedWars on its own server behind a proxy.

docs.title: First start
docs.text:
1. Download NewBedwars-<version>.jar from Modrinth and put it in plugins/.
  2. Start the server. NewBedwars creates its files in plugins/NewBedwars/.
  3. Stand at your lobby spawn and run /bw setLobby.
  4. Create your first arena: /bw arena create myArena. Continue with Arena setup.
  5. Players join with /bw join myArena, the arena selector or a join NPC.

docs.title: Files
docs.text:
Everything lives in plugins/NewBedwars/:

File or folder Contents config.yml Main settings (Configuration) modes.yml Game modes and game phases (Game modes and phases) language/*.yml Messages in every language; edit them or add your own language scoreboards.yml, bossBars.yml Scoreboards and boss bars of the waiting lobby, the game and the end of the game (Configuration) generators/*.yml Generator speeds and levels, one preset per game mode data/items.yml Shop items (Shop and upgrades) data/upgrades.yml Upgrade and trap prices per level data/guis/*.yml Shop and upgrade menus data/arenas/<name>.json Arena settings (written by the setup commands, with automatic backups) data/maps/<arena>/template/ Clean copy of every arena map, used to reset it after a game data/lobby.yml The lobby location (/bw setLobby) data/groups.json, data/npcs.json Arena groups and join NPCs data/backups/, data/exports/ Arena and config backups, and arena zips from /bw arena export data/playersData.json, data/playerStats.json Player data and stats (JSON by default, or MySQL, see Storage)

/bw reload reloads the configuration, messages, scoreboards, boss bars, generators, shop, GUIs and arenas without a server restart.

Warning

/bw reload stops every running game and kicks players who are in setup mode. Use it when the arenas are empty.

docs.title: Updating
docs.text:
NewBedwars checks Modrinth (GitHub as a fallback) for new versions every 12 hours. When one is out:

  • the console gets one line, and admins with newbedwars.update.notify get one chat line when they join;
  • /bw update checks right away, and /bw update download downloads the new jar (checksum verified) into plugins/update/. The server installs it on the next restart.

Updates.AutoDownload: true downloads new versions automatically. Updates.Channel chooses between release, beta and alpha versions, and Updates.Check: false turns the check off completely. Nothing about your server is sent. See Updates.

Tip

Versions up to 2.6-beta do not check for updates. Update to 2.7-beta once by hand; after that NewBedwars tells you about new versions itself.

Your configuration, arenas, maps and player data are kept when you update. New settings are added to config.yml with their default values, and data that has to move to a new format is moved automatically on the first start (the old files are kept as a backup). Read the changelog before updating.

docs.title: Network mode (Velocity)
docs.text:
Note: Network mode and the NewBedwars-Proxy plugin are available from 2.6-beta. Version 2.5-beta and older can not run on a network.

NewBedwars can run on a proxy network: lobby servers where players choose a game, and game servers that host the arenas. Players and parties are moved between them automatically.

By default (Network.Mode: NONE) NewBedwars is a single server and nothing on this page applies.

docs.title: What you need
docs.text:
Where What Velocity proxy NewBedwars-Proxy-<version>.jar in plugins/ (Velocity 4.x, Java 25) Every lobby and game server NewBedwars-<version>.jar (same version on all of them) Optional A MySQL/MariaDB database that game servers and the proxy can reach

Set up Velocity forwarding as usual (player-info-forwarding-mode = "MODERN" in velocity.toml, proxies.velocity in each Paper server's config/paper-global.yml).

Install the proxy plugin. Besides routing, it blocks players from sending fake NewBedwars network messages to your servers. Don't run Network.Mode: GAME/LOBBY without it.

docs.title: Scoreboard
docs.text: /server/ in scoreboards.yml shows the server's name (Network.ServerId); the default waiting scoreboard has a Server: line. A line with /server/ is left out on a single server. Existing scoreboards.yml files are not changed by an update: add the line yourself.

docs.title: Is MySQL required?
docs.text:
(For a single server see storage.md.)

No. Every feature works without a database, on one server or on a network. MySQL/MariaDB only adds:

Feature Without MySQL With MySQL Stats and player data (Storage.Type: MYSQL) Each server keeps its own stats, leaderboards and player settings in JSON files Shared by every server of the network Server status (Network.MySQL.Enabled on game servers + mysql: in the proxy config) The proxy only knows a game server's arenas while a player is online on it; a server it has not heard from is still tried and picks an arena itself The proxy always knows every game server's arenas, also right after a restart Rejoin notice on the lobby Works when somebody else is still online on that game server to carry the message Always works (the status table carries the rejoin places)

Joining through the proxy, parties, rejoining, map voting, RestartAfterGames, NPCs and placeholders all work without MySQL.

docs.title: Server config (plugins/NewBedwars/config.yml)
docs.text:
Network:
  Mode: GAME          # GAME on game servers, LOBBY on lobby servers
  ServerId: "game1"   # this server's name in velocity.toml [servers]
  LobbyServer: ""     # GAME: lobby to send players to; empty = the proxy picks the least full lobby
  LocalLobby: false   # GAME: false = no /bw setLobby needed on game servers (see below)
  LobbyJoinMessages: true  # LOBBY: show "<player> joined/left the game" (game servers never show it)
  RestartAfterGames: 0
  TicketTimeoutSeconds: 10
  StatePublishSeconds: 5
  MySQL:
    Enabled: false      # GAME: write the server status to the shared table (uses the MySQL section)
    HeartbeatSeconds: 5

Storage:
  Type: MYSQL           # share stats, leaderboards and languages across the network
MySQL:
  Host: "localhost"
  Port: 3306
  Database: "newbedwars"
  User: "root"
  Password: ""
  SslMode: PREFERRED              # DISABLED, PREFERRED, REQUIRED, VERIFY_CA or VERIFY_IDENTITY
  AllowPublicKeyRetrieval: false  # only for MySQL 8 without SSL; less secure

docs.title: Game servers (Mode: GAME)
docs.text:
• Set up arenas as on a single server. One server can host one or many arenas. Arena groups are not set here (see the lobby below); /bw group on a game server only lists them, and its own data/groups.json is not used.
  • No lobby needed (LocalLobby: false, default): players who arrive and wait for their arena, or who leave a game, wait for that moment invisibly in spectator mode at the world spawn, then go into the arena or on to a lobby server. With LocalLobby: true they are teleported to this server's /bw setLobby location instead (the old behaviour).
  • Players who arrive from the proxy go straight into the arena the proxy picked (parties together). A player who arrives without a join request is sent back to the lobby after TicketTimeoutSeconds. Staff with newbedwars.network.bypass (default: op) can stay, e.g. to set up arenas.
  • After a game (or /bw lobby), players go to a lobby server. With map voting, players who vote move to the next arena on the same server.
  • RestartAfterGames: <n> (0 = off): after n finished games the server is marked "restarting": the proxy and lobbies send no new players there, running games finish normally, and once no arena has players everyone left is sent to a lobby and the server shuts down. Your start script (or panel) has to start it again; the plugin only stops it. Useful to clear memory and old chunks of game servers that run for days.
  • Map voting across servers: at the end of a game the vote offers the free arenas of the same group on every game server (the item shows the server). If an arena on another server wins, everyone (parties together) is moved there through the proxy.

docs.title: Lobby servers (Mode: LOBBY)
docs.text:
• No arenas are loaded.
  • /bw join opens the arena selector with the arenas of all game servers; clicking an arena takes you to exactly that server's arena. /bw join <group|arena> asks the proxy for the best game: an arena name that exists on several servers means the fullest of them that has room. /bw join <server>:<arena> (and ARENA <server>:<arena> join NPCs) go only to that server's arena.
  • Arena groups are made here with /bw group (see commands.md). /bw group add <group> <arena> adds that arena on every game server that has it; /bw group add <group> <server>:<arena> only one server's arena. Problems and team sizes are checked against the arenas the game servers report. The proxy uses them right away for routing and the arena lists, also for game servers nobody is on, and sends them to every game server (each keeps the last copy in data/network-groups.json, so it still knows them after a restart); joining a group, its NPCs and placeholders and the map vote across servers all use them. With several lobby servers the last edit wins and is copied to the other lobbies.
  • /bw arena list shows the arenas of all game servers (server, group, state, players); /bw arena info explains how to set arenas up on a network. All other /bw arena subcommands (create, setup, backup, …) are refused here: run them on the game server that has the arena.
  • /bw spectate opens a menu of the running games on all game servers; /bw spectate <arena> watches that game.
  • Join NPCs: GROUP, ARENA and SELECTOR send players to game servers (the old NETWORK action was removed; NPCs that still have it work as GROUP). Holograms and the %newbedwars_group_<name>_...% placeholders show the network's numbers.
  • Only the party admin can join; the whole party is moved.

docs.title: Proxy config (plugins/newbedwars-proxy/config.yml)
docs.text:
game-servers: [game1, game2]   # names from velocity.toml
lobby-servers: [lobby]
ticket-timeout-seconds: 10
state-stale-seconds: 15
party-invite-seconds: 60
mysql:
  enabled: false
  host: "localhost"
  port: 3306
  database: "newbedwars"
  user: "root"
  password: ""
  ssl-mode: PREFERRED              # DISABLED, PREFERRED, REQUIRED, VERIFY_CA or VERIFY_IDENTITY
  allow-public-key-retrieval: false
  poll-seconds: 5
updates:
  check: true                      # false = never look for a new proxy version
  notify: true                     # one console line when a newer proxy version is out
  channel: BETA                    # RELEASE, BETA or ALPHA
  • The proxy picks the fullest arena that still has room (the same rule as /bw join on one server). If the game server refuses (the arena filled up in the meantime), the proxy tries one other server. If that fails too, the players go back to the lobby.
  • Game servers can only report their arenas while a player is online on them. A game server the proxy has not heard from recently is still tried, and it then picks an arena itself. With MySQL enabled on the game servers and on the proxy, the proxy always knows every server's arenas.
  • If game-servers is not empty, the proxy only accepts arena states (plugin messages and MySQL rows) from those servers; anything else is ignored and logged once. With an empty list the proxy learns game servers from what they report (at most 128). A server that has been silent for ten times state-stale-seconds is forgotten until it reports again.
  • MySQL rows carry the game server's own clock, so the proxy never compares it with its clock: a server counts as alive when its row's heartbeat changes between two polls.
  • Incoming data is size-limited (64 arenas per server, names up to 64 characters, 256 rejoin places per server, 128 servers). When the network state for the lobbies would not fit one plugin message, rejoin data is left out first, then the least useful arenas (running and empty ones) are cut, and the proxy logs it once.
  • A player who just sent a join request cannot start another one for about 2 seconds (lobby servers also wait 1 second between requests). Join tickets carry a relative lifetime, so differing clocks between proxy and game servers do not matter.
  • The proxy checks for new versions of itself like the Paper plugin does (see Updates). It only writes a console line and shows the result in /nbwproxy; it never downloads anything.
  • /nbwproxy (permission newbedwars.proxy.admin) lists the game servers and arenas the proxy knows.
  • Proxy texts are in plugins/newbedwars-proxy/lang/en.yml and pl.yml and are chosen by the player's client language.

docs.title: Stats and player data
docs.text: With Storage.Type: MYSQL on every server (same database), stats, leaderboards (/bw leaderboard, placeholders), languages and quick-buy layouts are shared by the whole network. A game's result is added to the stats on the database, so games ending on several servers at once never overwrite each other. A player's data is read when they join a server; leaderboards and online players' stats are refreshed every minute. On the first start with an empty database, that server's JSON data is imported once.

docs.title: Rejoining
docs.text: When a player leaves a running game while their team is still playing (disconnect or /bw lobby), the game server keeps their place for RejoinTime minutes and tells the network about it. On a lobby server the player gets a title, a sound, a clickable "Click to rejoin" button and an action bar reminder with the time left. /bw rejoin (or the button) sends them back to that game server and arena. A player who was the last of their team has no place to go back to (their team is out).

docs.title: Parties
docs.text: In network mode, /party (alias /p) is handled by the proxy, so parties survive server switches. The commands are the same as on a single server.

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
• Firewall your backend servers (lobby and game) from the internet and only let the proxy reach them. With Velocity modern forwarding the forwarding secret is the only thing that stops someone from connecting to a backend directly and claiming any identity. Keep forwarding.secret private and never expose backend ports.
  • The proxy never forwards the newbedwars:main plugin channel from players to servers, so clients cannot forge join tickets or party data. Messages from a backend are checked against the sending player's connection, the sender's role (only lobbies define groups) and the size limits above.
  • MySQL: ssl-mode defaults to PREFERRED (encrypt when the server supports it, no certificate check). For a database on another machine use REQUIRED, or VERIFY_CA / VERIFY_IDENTITY with a trusted certificate, and a dedicated database user that only has access to the NewBedwars database. Only game servers and the proxy need the nbw_servers table; treat the credentials in config.yml as secrets.
  • Hardening added in 2.6-beta: a join request is only accepted for the player who sent it (target at most 64 characters); a game server can only move players that are on it; join tickets expire and a lobby allows one join request per player per second; the proxy drops oversized or malformed messages and reserves arena slots only until the real state arrives; when game-servers is set in the proxy config, states from other servers are ignored (and logged once); the proxy only reads the first 256 nbw_servers rows. The proxy config and item/GUI YAML are loaded with a safe loader (no !!java tags), and /bw arena import limits unpacked size to 2 GB.
  • MySQL: MySQL.AllowPublicKeyRetrieval (proxy: allow-public-key-retrieval) defaults to false. If the connection fails after updating with a caching_sha2_password user and no SSL, set it to true or use ssl-mode: REQUIRED.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text: • BungeeCord is not supported yet (Velocity only).

docs.title: Web panel (NewBedwars-Panel)
docs.text:
Note

The panel needs NewBedwars 2.8-beta or newer on the same server.

NewBedwars-Panel is a separate addon jar that adds a browser admin panel to your server. With it you can:

  • watch every arena live: its state, players, phase (with the time left and the next phase), game time, and each team's bed;
  • see every game mode and apply one to a waiting arena (game modes);
  • control running games: start the countdown, start now, end as a draw, stop and reset, skip to the next phase, and send a message to everyone in the arena;
  • read each arena's game log: joins and leaves, chat and team chat, kills and final kills, beds, phases, generator upgrades, eliminated teams and admin actions, updated live;
  • look up any player's stats and the leaderboards (top 10, 25 or 100 by wins, kills, final kills, beds, deaths, losses or games);
  • see online players, TPS and memory;
  • enable, disable, back up, restore, reset, copy, export (download) and delete arenas;
  • import arena zips you upload;
  • on a network, manage the arenas, shops and stats of every game server from the lobby's panel with one login (network mode).

Each person logs in with their own account. What they may do depends on their role, and every action is written to an activity log.

The panel runs inside the Paper server (no extra program, no database). It speaks HTTPS by default.

  • Using your own certificate
  • Behind a reverse proxy (nginx, Caddy)
