docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
1. Put NewBedwars-Panel-<version>.jar next to NewBedwars-<version>.jar in plugins/. Use the same version for both.
  2. Start the server. The console shows something like: 
    [NewBedwars-Panel] Panel running at https://localhost:8150/
[NewBedwars-Panel] No panel accounts yet. Create the first admin with: nbwpanel user create <name> admin
[NewBedwars-Panel] Created a self-signed certificate, SHA-256 fingerprint: 83:3E:87:...
  3. Open port 8150 (TCP) in your firewall or hosting panel if you want to reach the panel from another computer.

Requirements:

  • Paper 1.17 to 26.x with NewBedwars 2.8-beta or newer.
  • A Java runtime with the built-in web server (module jdk.httpserver). Standard JDK/JRE builds (e.g. Eclipse Temurin) have it. Only stripped-down custom runtimes made with jlink may lack it. In that case the console says so and the panel stays off.

Changes to plugins/NewBedwars-Panel/config.yml take effect after a server restart.

docs.title: The first admin account
docs.text:
Accounts are created from the server console, or in game by an op with newbedwars.panel.manage:

nbwpanel user create Alex admin

The answer contains a one-time password, shown only this once:

[NBW Panel] Account Alex created with role admin.
[NBW Panel] One-time password: xB7VZkhaJktRwFpt
[NBW Panel] It works once: the panel asks for a new password at the first login. It is not shown again.

Log in with it. The panel then asks you to choose your own password (10 to 128 characters) before anything else can be used. After that, create further accounts in the panel under Accounts, or with the same command.

If somebody forgets their password, run nbwpanel user reset <name>, or click New password in the panel. They get a new one-time password and are logged out everywhere.

docs.title: Logging in and the certificate warning
docs.text:
Open https://<your-server-address>:8150/. By default the panel uses a self-signed certificate, so the browser warns once ("Your connection is not private" / "Potential security risk").

  • To make sure you are talking to your own server, compare the SHA-256 fingerprint in the browser's certificate details with the one in the console or in nbwpanel status. If they match, accept the warning.
  • If you reach the panel through a domain name or a public IP, add it to Https.Hostnames so the certificate lists it.
  • To get rid of the warning completely, use your own certificate or a reverse proxy.

The self-signed certificate is valid for 397 days. It is renewed automatically 30 days before it expires, and whenever Https.Hostnames or Bind changes. The fingerprint changes then, so the browser warns again.

The panel is in English and Polish. It follows the browser language, and you can switch it with the language selector in the top bar. DefaultLanguage is used when the browser asks for neither.

docs.title: Accounts and roles
docs.text:
Every account has one role. Two roles are built in and can not be changed:

Role Can admin everything staff view the arenas and players and the player stats, also on the other servers of the network (dashboard.view, stats.view, network.servers)

Under Roles, admins (or anyone with roles.manage) can create their own roles from these permissions:

Permission Allows dashboard.view the arena list, arena details, online players, TPS and memory arena.enable / arena.disable enabling / disabling arenas (disabling sends waiting players out) arena.backup making backups and seeing the backup list arena.restore restoring a backup arena.resetmap putting the map back to its saved state arena.export exporting arenas and downloading the zip files arena.import uploading and importing arena zips arena.copy copying an arena arena.delete deleting an arena (file, world and saved map; backups are kept) users.manage creating accounts, new passwords, changing roles, deleting accounts roles.manage creating, changing and deleting roles audit.view the activity log stats.view player stats and leaderboards game.manage start, stop, skip phases of games and broadcast to an arena (like /bw game) modes.view the Modes tab of the shop editor and the Mode column on Shop > Arenas. The built-in admin role has it, staff does not modes.apply applying a game mode to an arena (the picker and Apply button on Shop > Arenas; only while the arena is waiting for players). Needs modes.view to be usable. The built-in admin role has it, staff does not modes.edit creating, editing and deleting game modes, phase lists and generator configs on the Modes tab (see game modes). Needs modes.view to be usable. The built-in admin role has it, staff does not. Not local-only: on a network it works on every game server through the gateway shop.edit the shop editor: items, their texts, shop GUIs and which GUIs the arenas use shop.commands changing the commands of shop items (Run commands, onBuyEvent: COMMANDS) and the permission an item gives (Give a permission for the game, GIVE_PERM), and switching an item's action to or from those two. Commands run as the server console and a given permission can be any permission, so this gives full control of the server: give it only to people you would give console access. Without it, both fields are shown read-only and the action can not be switched network.servers on a gateway panel: the server list and everything on the other servers of the network (what you may do there still depends on your other permissions). Never forwarded to other servers game.log the game log of each arena. It includes team chat, so give it only to people who may read that

Rules that always apply:

  • Every permission is checked by the server, not just hidden in the page.
  • Nobody can give an account or a role a permission they don't have themselves. They also can't change accounts or roles that have more permissions than they do. Someone with only users.manage therefore can't make themselves an admin.
  • The last admin account can't be deleted or given another role.
  • A role that is still assigned to an account can't be deleted.
  • Arena actions follow the same rules as /bw arena. For example, an arena with players in it can't be disabled. A refused action shows the plugin's own message.

docs.title: Game modes
docs.text:
The Modes tab (Shop > Modes, #/shop/modes, permission modes.view) lists every game mode with its settings (generator preset, game phases, shop and upgrade menu, players per team, team count), a tag for the built-in ones and the timeline of its game phases. Without the permission modes.edit they are read-only here: change them in modes.yml (see Game modes and phases) or ask an admin. The shop editor itself still needs shop.edit to open.

With the permission modes.edit the Modes tab becomes an editor and the changes are written to the server's files and reloaded at once:

  • Modes: New mode, and Edit / Delete on each mode. A mode picks a generator config, a phase list, a shop and an upgrade menu (each can stay "unchanged") and the players per team and team count (0 = unchanged). Built-in modes can be edited but not deleted. Arenas that already got a mode keep their copy.
  • Phase lists: each phase has a name, a duration typed as mm:ss and a list of actions chosen from the known ones (generator upgrades with a level, bed destruction, Ender Dragons, game end, ...). Phases can be added, removed and moved up and down. The built-in lists cannot be deleted.
  • Generator configs: the YAML of a generator preset in a text box. New generator config asks for a name and which config to copy from; the ConfigurationId line is set to the new name for you. The ConfigurationId must equal the name. The text is limited to 48 KB. The built-in configs can be edited but not deleted.

A phase list or generator config that a mode or an arena still uses cannot be deleted; the panel lists who uses it. If the server rejects a change as invalid, the reasons are shown under the form. Every change is written to the activity log (modes.save, modes.delete, phases.save, phases.delete, generators.save, generators.delete).

Shop > Arenas (#/shop/arenas) has a Mode column with each arena's mode and, under it, its generator config, phase list and team count x players per team. The mode is worked out from the arena's current settings: it is the mode whose settings all match, otherwise the arena shows Custom.

With the permission modes.apply each row also has a mode picker and an Apply button. It copies the mode into the arena once, like /bw setMode, and works only while the arena is waiting for players; the shop and upgrade menu pickers of the row then show the new menus. The panel warns when the arena's team count differs from the mode's. If the mode names something that doesn't exist (a generator file, phase list or menu), nothing is changed and the missing names are shown.

The dashboard lines the team columns up for arenas with different team counts. The Group arenas selector groups the list by team format (teams x players per team, e.g. "4 x 4 · 16 players"); the browser remembers your choice.

docs.title: Game control and game log
docs.text:
On an arena's page, Game shows only the actions that fit the arena's state (waiting: start countdown, start now; starting: start now, stop; playing: skip phase, end as a draw, stop and reset; ending: stop). Ending as a draw saves the stats; "stop and reset" sends everyone out at once. Messages players see name the panel user (Panel: Alex). A broadcast may use & colour codes (up to 256 characters); in game, /bw game broadcast <message> does the same.

The game log is kept in memory only: a finished game stays readable until the next game in that arena starts, and it is lost when the server restarts. Filter it by chat, kills and beds, game events, joins and leaves, and admin actions.

Commands typed by anyone in an arena's world (players, spectators, admins in setup or just visiting) are shown under Admin and commands, e.g. /bw game forcestart or /gamemode creative, also when the command was refused (marked "no permission" when the player lacks the command's permission, "cancelled" when another plugin stopped it). Player commands from GameLog.IgnoredCommands (leaving, language, party, private messages, ...) are left out, and login and password commands (/login, /register, /changepassword, ...) are never logged.

docs.title: Shop editor
docs.text:
Shop (permission shop.edit) has four tabs:

  • Items: every item of plugins/NewBedwars/data/items.yml. An item has a material, amount, price and currency, what buying it does (give the item, armor or a tool, buy a team upgrade, or nothing for decoration), its item logic (TNT, fireball, bridge egg, ... and addon logic), enchantments, item flags, an optional permission and "permanent". Under Texts you set the display name, the shop icon description and the lore of the bought item for each language, with & colour codes and a preview. The texts are stored in the language files (CustomItemsNames). A new item's name can't be changed later.
  • GUIs: the shop and upgrade menus in data/guis/. The grid shows every slot of the inventory; header and footer rows (darker) are shown on every page, the rows between them show the home page or the open category. Drag an entry from the palette onto a slot, drag slots to swap them, or select a slot and choose what it shows on the right (arrow keys move, Delete empties). Categories are buttons that open a page with their items in the order you set; the category home is the start page. Price overrides give an upgrade GUI its own prices for some upgrades: arenas whose upgrade shop opens this GUI use them instead of the prices from the Upgrades tab (for example cheaper upgrades for solo arenas). Item prices do the same for shop items: arenas whose shop opens this GUI (or a menu opened from it) use the price, currency and amount listed there instead of the item's own; leave the currency or amount empty to keep the item's value.
  • Upgrades: the prices of every team upgrade and trap (data/upgrades.yml). Each row is one level the team can buy, in order, with its own price and currency (iron, gold, diamond or emerald). Fewer rows mean fewer levels, no rows means the upgrade can't be bought; each upgrade shows how many levels it supports at most. Upgrade icons in the Items tab have no price of their own: buying them always uses these prices.
  • Arenas: which GUI the item shop and the upgrade shop of each arena open. Only arenas that are waiting can be changed.

Changes apply at once: players see them the next time they open a shop, no /bw reload. Items and GUIs that are still used (by a GUI, an arena or config.yml) can't be deleted; the page says where they are used. Every save keeps the previous file in plugins/NewBedwars/data/backups/shop/ (items/, guis/<id>/, upgrades/, language/<code>/, as many as Backups.Keep).

References a GUI file already had but that can't be resolved on this server (for example an item that failed to load) are listed at the top and kept unchanged when you save; new references must be valid. Saving a GUI from the panel rewrites its file without the comments it had.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
Permission newbedwars.panel.manage (default: op). The console can always use them. In game, user create, user reset, user delete and network forget also need op, even when a permissions plugin gives newbedwars.panel.manage to someone else. Command blocks and other senders that are neither the console nor a player can not use them.

Command Does /nbwpanel status panel address, certificate (self-signed fingerprint, own keystore or plain HTTP), number of accounts, logged-in sessions /nbwpanel user create <name> <role> creates an account and prints its one-time password /nbwpanel user reset <name> new one-time password; the account is logged out /nbwpanel user delete <name> deletes the account and logs it out (not the last admin) /nbwpanel user list all accounts with their role; marks passwords that were not changed yet /nbwpanel network status the panel's network role and, on a gateway, every server with its status and how its certificate is trusted /nbwpanel network secret prints a new random Network.Secret (it is not saved anywhere) /nbwpanel network forget <server> gateway: forgets the remembered certificate of a server, so the next connection trusts the certificate it sees (console or op only)

Account names have 3 to 32 characters: letters, digits, _, . and -. They are not case-sensitive.

The chat and console messages are in plugins/NewBedwars-Panel/lang/en.yml and pl.yml. You can edit them. Players get their game language and the console gets DefaultLanguage.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
plugins/NewBedwars-Panel/config.yml:

Key Default Meaning Bind 0.0.0.0 Network address to listen on. 0.0.0.0 = all; 127.0.0.1 = only this machine (use it behind a reverse proxy on the same machine) Port 8150 TCP port Https.Enabled true false = plain HTTP. Only use it behind a reverse proxy that adds HTTPS, or on a trusted network. The console warns about it Https.Keystore "" Your own PKCS12 (.p12/.pfx) or JKS keystore, relative to the panel folder. Empty = self-signed certificate Https.KeystorePassword "" Its password Https.Hostnames [] Extra domain names / IPs for the self-signed certificate (localhost and the Bind address are always included) TrustProxyHeaders false true only behind your own reverse proxy: the client IP is taken from X-Forwarded-For, HTTPS from X-Forwarded-Proto and the host from X-Forwarded-Host Session.IdleMinutes 30 Logged out after this long without activity Session.MaxHours 12 Logged out after this long in any case Login.MaxAttempts 5 Wrong passwords before the account and the address are locked Login.LockMinutes 10 How long the lock lasts Upload.MaxMegabytes 512 Largest arena zip that can be uploaded DefaultLanguage en en or pl, used when the browser or the console has no other choice Network.Role STANDALONE STANDALONE, GATEWAY or NODE, see Network mode Network.Id "" Name of this server in the network (letters, digits, _ -). Empty = the NewBedwars server id. On a node it must match the node's key under Network.Peers on the gateway. Shown as user@<id> in the activity logs of the other servers Network.Secret "" Shared secret, at least 32 characters, the same on the gateway and every node Network.NodeLogin false NODE only: true also allows logging in to this node directly with its own accounts Network.Peers {} GATEWAY only: the other panels (<server id>: {Url, Fingerprint}) GameLog.IgnoredCommands player commands (lobby, lang, party, msg, bw lobby, ...) Commands typed in an arena world that are not shown in the game log. A two-word entry like bw lobby leaves out only that subcommand

docs.title: Using your own certificate
docs.text:
If you already have a certificate for a domain that points to your server (for example from Let's Encrypt), turn it into a PKCS12 file:

openssl pkcs12 -export -in fullchain.pem -inkey privkey.pem -out panel.p12 -name panel -passout pass:CHANGE_ME

Put panel.p12 into plugins/NewBedwars-Panel/ and set:

Https:
  Enabled: true
  Keystore: "panel.p12"
  KeystorePassword: "CHANGE_ME"

Restart the server and open https://your.domain:8150/. Let's Encrypt certificates last 90 days: create the .p12 again after each renewal and restart. If that is too much work, use a reverse proxy instead. With a real certificate the panel also sends Strict-Transport-Security.

docs.title: Behind a reverse proxy (nginx, Caddy)
docs.text:
A reverse proxy on the same machine can give the panel a normal https://panel.example.com address with an automatically renewed certificate. Let the panel listen only locally, over plain HTTP:

Bind: 127.0.0.1
Port: 8150
Https:
  Enabled: false
TrustProxyHeaders: true

nginx:

server {
    listen 443 ssl;
    server_name panel.example.com;
    # ssl_certificate / ssl_certificate_key as usual

    client_max_body_size 512m;   # at least Upload.MaxMegabytes

    location / {
        proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:8150;
        proxy_set_header Host $host;
        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $remote_addr;
        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto https;
        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Host $host;
        proxy_read_timeout 600s;   # exports and imports of big maps can take a while
    }
}

Caddy:

panel.example.com {
    reverse_proxy 127.0.0.1:8150
}

Caddy sets the forwarding headers itself.

Warning

Turn on TrustProxyHeaders only when the panel port can't be reached directly (Bind: 127.0.0.1, or a firewall). Otherwise anyone can fake their IP address and get around the login lock.

Set X-Forwarded-For to the client address ($remote_addr), not by appending to an incoming header. The panel uses the last address in the header.

The panel closes connections that send a request more slowly than 10 seconds (30 seconds without data during an upload). A reverse proxy also protects it from many slow connections at once, because it receives the whole request before passing it on.

docs.title: Network mode
docs.text:
By default a panel only controls the server it is installed on. On a network (see network.md) you can instead log in once, on the lobby server's panel, and work with every game server from there.

  • Lobby server (the gateway): Network.Role: GATEWAY. Its dashboard shows every server (status, players, TPS, arenas) and one arena list for all of them. Arena pages, the game log, the shop editor, stats and arena import/export work for any server, picked by the server tag, the arena link or the Server selector.
  • Game servers (the nodes): Network.Role: NODE. A node answers only its gateway. It has no login of its own unless you set Network.NodeLogin: true.
  • In the shop editor, the Sync items, Sync GUIs and Sync upgrade prices buttons (Items, GUIs and Upgrades tabs) copy the items, GUIs or upgrade prices of the selected server to every other online server. They only run when pressed; same-named entries are overwritten and entries that exist only on the other servers are kept. Sync the items before the GUIs.
  • Servers that do not answer are shown as offline on the dashboard (their arenas get an offline badge and the player count shows –).
  • Everything else (accounts, roles, the activity log) stays on the gateway. People can't use it to change the accounts of a node.
  • On a lobby server (Network.Mode: LOBBY) the dashboard also lists arenas of servers without a panel link, read-only, as "Not connected".

Without a Network.Role (or with STANDALONE) nothing changes: one panel per server with its own accounts, as before.

docs.title: Setting it up
docs.text:
1. Install NewBedwars-Panel on the lobby server and on every game server. The panel is a Paper plugin only: nothing is installed on the Velocity proxy, and the panels talk to each other directly over HTTPS, not through the proxy. Each panel needs its own Port if they share a machine (for example 8150, 8151, 8152), and the gateway must be able to reach the nodes' ports. Keep node ports closed to everyone else (firewall, private network).
  2. Make a secret: run /nbwpanel network secret on any server and copy the result.
  3. On every game server, in plugins/NewBedwars-Panel/config.yml:
Network:
  Role: NODE
  Secret: "<the secret>"
  1. On the lobby server:
Network:
  Role: GATEWAY
  Secret: "<the same secret>"
  Peers:
    game1:
      Url: "https://10.0.0.5:8151"
      Fingerprint: ""
    game2:
      Url: "https://10.0.0.6:8151"
      Fingerprint: ""

The keys under Peers are the server ids the proxy uses (the same names shown in /bw join on the lobby), and must be the same as each node's own id (its Network.Id, or its NewBedwars server id when Network.Id is empty). A node refuses requests meant for another server and says so in its console. The dashboard marks servers in the network list that have no Peers entry as "Not connected".

  1. Restart the servers (panel changes need a restart), create the accounts on the gateway (/nbwpanel user create <name> <role>), and give roles that should reach other servers the network.servers permission. Check with /nbwpanel network status.

docs.title: How the servers trust each other
docs.text:
• The secret. Every request from the gateway to a node is signed with the secret (HMAC-SHA256) over the request, the time, a one-time number, the user, the user's permissions, the user's IP address, the target server and the body. A node refuses anything unsigned, changed, older or newer than a minute, or seen before. Without the secret nobody can talk to a node's panel, even if its port is open. Keep it as private as a database password, and use a different one per network.
  • Permissions. The gateway checks what the user may do, and sends the permissions along; the node checks them again. users.manage, roles.manage, audit.view and network.servers are never accepted by a node.
  • Activity log. The node records every action as name@<gateway id> with the user's IP address, in its own audit.log.
  • Certificates. Panels use self-signed certificates by default, so the gateway does not use the normal certificate check for nodes. Instead it remembers the certificate it sees the first time (peers.json, shown by /nbwpanel network status) and refuses the server if the certificate ever changes (the server then shows "Certificate changed"). After a change you made on purpose run /nbwpanel network forget <server>. To skip trust-on-first-use, put the node's SHA-256 fingerprint (shown in its console at start, or by /nbwpanel status) in Fingerprint. A node with a normal CA-signed certificate (for example Let's Encrypt behind a reverse proxy) can use Fingerprint: system.
  • Plain HTTP. http:// URLs work but anything on the way can read the traffic (the secret itself is never sent), and uploaded arena files are not covered by the signature. The gateway warns about it at start. Use them only when both panels are on the same machine or a trusted private network.
  • Uploads. Arena zips uploaded to another server are streamed straight through the gateway; their content is not covered by the signature (the user, the target and the time are).
  • Clocks. The two servers' clocks must be within one minute of each other, or the node answers "rejected".

docs.title: Status values
docs.text: Status Meaning Online answers Offline not reachable or no answer in time (the page shows the last known state in grey) Rejected the node refused the gateway: wrong Network.Secret, clocks too far apart, its Peers key differs from the node's id, or the node's panel is not a NODE Certificate changed the certificate differs from the remembered one, see above Not connected the server is in the network list but has no Peers entry

docs.title: Files and backups
docs.text:
Everything is in plugins/NewBedwars-Panel/:

File Contents config.yml settings accounts.dat accounts and roles, encrypted (AES-GCM). Passwords are stored only as PBKDF2 hashes panel.key the 32-byte key for accounts.dat (owner read/write only, where the system supports it) selfsigned.p12 the self-signed certificate and its private key audit.log the activity log, one JSON line per action (moved to audit.log.1 at server start once it is over 5 MB) lang/en.yml, lang/pl.yml command messages

Back up accounts.dat and panel.key together. One without the other is useless. A lost panel.key means the accounts can't be read: delete accounts.dat and create the admin again with nbwpanel user create.

Instead of the file, the key can come from the environment variable NBW_PANEL_KEY (32 bytes, Base64, e.g. openssl rand -base64 32). The key then never lies next to the data. panel.key is not created or used while the variable is set.

Shop editor saves keep the previous version of items.yml, upgrades.yml, the GUI files and the language files in plugins/NewBedwars/data/backups/shop/.

Exports and uploaded imports are kept in plugins/NewBedwars/data/exports/, the same folder as /bw arena export and /bw arena import. Arena backups are in plugins/NewBedwars/data/backups/.

docs.title: Security notes
docs.text:
• Keep HTTPS on, or put a reverse proxy with HTTPS in front. Over plain HTTP, passwords and session cookies can be read on the network.
  • If only you need the panel, bind it to 127.0.0.1 and reach it through an SSH tunnel: ssh -L 8150:127.0.0.1:8150 you@server, then open https://localhost:8150/.
  • Give people the smallest role that does the job. staff can only look (it may look at every server of the network).
  • Sessions use an HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict cookie (__Host-nbw over HTTPS). Every change needs a CSRF token, and requests from other websites are refused.
  • The page itself loads nothing from other sites (no CDN, no fonts, no tracking) and forbids being embedded in frames.
  • On a network, the secret is the key to every game server's panel. Keep config.yml private and don't expose node ports.
  • Check Activity (or audit.log) now and then. Failed and locked logins are recorded with the IP address.
  • Bind: 0.0.0.0 makes the panel reachable from every network the server is on. If it doesn't have to be public, allow port 8150 only from your own IP in the firewall. The built-in web server has no protection against clients that keep many slow connections open, so a reverse proxy (nginx, Caddy) in front is the better choice for a panel that is open to the internet. The game itself is never slowed down by the panel.
  • Enable TrustProxyHeaders only behind your own reverse proxy. Otherwise anyone can fake their IP address, and with it the login lock.
  • Arena imports (upload and unzip) are limited to Upload.MaxMegabytes, 2 GB unpacked and 200 000 files, and files can only be written inside the server's export and map folders.
  • Network mode uses one shared secret. Anyone who has it (for example from a game server whose files leaked) can send signed requests to every other server's panel with any permission except the local-only ones. Treat every server that has the secret as trusted, keep node panels reachable only from the gateway, and change the secret (/nbwpanel network secret on one server, then on all) if one server is compromised.
  • Between the gateway and the game servers, use HTTPS (the default). The contents of an arena zip sent to another server are not covered by the request signature, only by the encrypted connection.
  • The login lock counts failed attempts per IP address and per account. Someone who knows an account name can lock it for 10 minutes by guessing wrong 5 times. Behind a reverse proxy without TrustProxyHeaders, every visitor shares one IP address, so failed logins of anyone count for everyone.
  • Commands typed in an arena world are shown in the game log. /login, /register and similar are never logged, but other plugins may have their own secret commands (for example 2FA codes): add them to GameLog.IgnoredCommands.
  • The shop.commands permission lets a role make shop items that run console commands or give any permission (this includes switching an item's action to or from those two). Give it only to people you would give console access.
  • The arena.import permission is trusted like console access. An imported map is not scanned or stripped: it can contain command blocks (they run when enable-command-block=true in server.properties) and datapacks. Give it only to people you would give console access. The same goes for /bw arena import (newbedwars.bw.arena.import).
  • If the pinned certificate file of the network peers (peers.json) is damaged, the panel moves it aside as peers.json.corrupt-<time>, logs a SEVERE message and refuses contact with the peers it can no longer verify. Check the peers' certificate fingerprints, then run /nbwpanel network forget <peer> to trust a peer again. The pins that could still be read are written back to a fresh peers.json, and a marker file peers.json.locked keeps this protection active after a restart: peers without a pin are refused until you release each one with forget. The lock stays until you delete peers.json.locked yourself (only do that after you checked every peer's fingerprint).

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Problem Fix port 8150 on 0.0.0.0 is already in use Another program (or a second server) uses the port: change Port This Java runtime has no built-in web server Run the server with a full JDK/JRE (e.g. Temurin) accounts.dat can not be read with this key panel.key / NBW_PANEL_KEY is not the key the file was written with. Restore the matching key, or delete accounts.dat and create the accounts again The browser can't connect Open the port in the firewall / hosting panel; check Bind; use https://, not http:// "Too many wrong tries" Wait Login.LockMinutes, or reset the password from the console Upload fails with "larger than the upload limit" Raise Upload.MaxMegabytes (and client_max_body_size in nginx) A server is "Rejected" Different Network.Secret, clocks more than a minute apart, the Peers key on the gateway is not the node's id (the node's console names both), or Network.Role on that server is not NODE (check its console at start) A server is "Certificate changed" Its certificate was recreated (deleted selfsigned.p12, new IP in Https.Hostnames, ...). If that was you, run /nbwpanel network forget <server> on the gateway A server is "Offline" Wrong Url/port, the node's panel is not running, or a firewall blocks the gateway Network.Role is GATEWAY but Network.Secret is missing Set a Network.Secret of 32+ characters on every server; until then the panel runs as a standalone panel Uploads fail behind a reverse proxy but work directly The proxy's body size limit or timeout is too low (see the nginx example)

docs.title: In shop items
docs.text: (2.8-beta) Placeholders also work the other way round: the shop names and descriptions of shop items, upgrades and traps, and the names and descriptions of menu categories can use any PlaceholderAPI placeholder, and the player who opens the menu sees their own values. The item a player receives when buying keeps its normal text on purpose, so bought blocks still stack. See Shop items.

docs.title: Shop and upgrades
docs.text:
The shop is made of three kinds of files in plugins/NewBedwars/data/:

File Contents items.yml Every item that can be sold: material, amount, price, what buying does guis/*.yml Shop and upgrade menus: which item goes into which slot, categories upgrades.yml Upgrade and trap prices per level

Run /bw reload after editing these files (it stops running games, see Installation).

Easier with the web panel

The web panel addon has a visual editor for all three: items with a live colour preview, menus on a drag-and-drop slot grid, and upgrade prices. Changes apply at once and the previous version of every file is backed up.

docs.title: Shop items (items.yml)
docs.text:
Every entry is one item. The key is the item ID that menus refer to:

TNT:
  material: TNT
  amount: 1
  price: 4
  priceType: GOLD
  onBuyEvent: GIVE_ITEM
  itemLogic: TNT
  isPermanent: false
  permission: ''
  description: default
  iconDesc: default
  enchantments: {}
  itemFlags: []
Key Meaning material Bukkit material name of the item amount How many the player gets price / priceType Cost and currency: IRON, GOLD, DIAMOND, EMERALD, NONE (free), or OTHER (paid with the item in priceMaterial) priceMaterial Only for priceType: OTHER: the item players pay with, for example NETHER_STAR onBuyEvent What buying does: GIVE_ITEM (into the inventory), GIVE_ARMOR (upgrade the armor tier), GIVE_TOOL (sword or tool that follows the tool rules), UPGRADE (a team upgrade icon), COMMANDS, OPEN_GUI and GIVE_PERM (see Commands, menus and permissions), CANCEL (nothing, for decoration) commands / gui / givePermission Only for COMMANDS, OPEN_GUI and GIVE_PERM, see below itemLogic Special behaviour when the item is used: NONE, TNT, FIREBALL, BRIDGE_EGG, LUCKY_BLOCK, POTION, BLAST_PROTECTION, IRON_GOLEM, SILVERFISH, PORTABLE_TOWER. Addons can add their own isPermanent The item is unbreakable. A GIVE_ITEM item is also given back on every respawn once bought. See Permanent items permission Only players with this permission can buy it (empty = everyone) description / iconDesc default takes the name and shop description from the language files (CustomItemsNames section: <ID>-name and <ID>-icon-description) enchantments Enchantments and levels, for example {SHARPNESS: 1} itemFlags Item flags, for example [HIDE_ENCHANTS]

PlaceholderAPI (2.8-beta): when PlaceholderAPI is installed, placeholders are filled in for the player who opens the menu, for example &7You have won %newbedwars_stat_wins% games. This works in:

  • the shop name and shop description of shop items (<ID>-name and <ID>-icon-description),
  • the same texts of team upgrades and traps in the upgrade menu,
  • the Name and Description of categories in menu files.

Any PlaceholderAPI placeholder works, also those of other plugins. The menu shows the values from the moment it was opened.

Note

Placeholders are only filled in on the icons in the menus. The item a player receives when buying keeps its normal name and description, on purpose: with player-specific texts, bought blocks such as wool would no longer stack with each other. Put placeholders in <ID>-icon-description, not in the item's own description.

An item with an unknown material, enchantment or flag (for example from a newer Minecraft version) is skipped with a console warning and kept in the file unchanged. The same happens to an item with priceType: OTHER and no valid priceMaterial, and to a COMMANDS, OPEN_GUI or GIVE_PERM item without its commands, gui or givePermission.

docs.title: Commands, menus and permissions
docs.text:
Three onBuyEvent values do something other than give an item. The price is taken first, as for every item.

VipKit:
  material: NETHER_STAR
  price: 1
  priceType: OTHER
  priceMaterial: DIAMOND_BLOCK
  onBuyEvent: COMMANDS
  commands:
  - give {player} golden_apple 2
  - 'player: kit vip'
Specials:
  material: CHEST
  price: 0
  priceType: NONE
  onBuyEvent: OPEN_GUI
  gui: specialShop
DoubleJump:
  material: FEATHER
  price: 8
  priceType: EMERALD
  onBuyEvent: GIVE_PERM
  givePermission: doublejump.use
  • COMMANDS runs every line of commands (without the /). Lines run as the console, so they can do anything the console can; a line that starts with player: runs as the buyer instead. {player}, {team} and {arena} are replaced with the buyer's name, team and arena.
  • OPEN_GUI opens the shop menu whose GuiId is in gui. With price 0 it works as a link to another menu, and no "bought" message is shown.
  • GIVE_PERM gives the buyer the permission in givePermission until they leave the game, are eliminated or the game ends. It can't be bought twice in one game. Use it for perks of other plugins that check a permission.

docs.title: Permanent items
docs.text:
What a player keeps after death depends on onBuyEvent, not only on isPermanent:

onBuyEvent Kept after death What isPermanent does GIVE_ITEM Only when isPermanent: true Unbreakable, and given back on every respawn GIVE_TOOL (swords) Gamerule MakeSwordsPermanent (false = back to the starting sword) Unbreakable only GIVE_TOOL (pickaxe, axe, shears) Gamerule MakeToolsPermanent (false = lost) Unbreakable only GIVE_TOOL (any other material) Always Unbreakable only GIVE_ARMOR Always (the armor tier stays) Nothing

The gamerules have their defaults in config.yml and can be changed per arena with /bw gamerule (advanced setup mode).

The starting sword is the item named in BasicSword in config.yml.

docs.title: Shop and upgrade menus (guis/*.yml)
docs.text:
On the first start, exampleShop.yml and exampleUpgrade.yml are copied into data/guis/. Edit those copies, or copy one to make a new menu with another GuiId.

GuiId: exampleShop
GuiClass: ShopGUI
GuiName: "Example Shop"
Size: 54
Fill: ci:fill
Empty: empty
HeaderSize: 18
FooterSize: 9

Slots:
  1: category:home
  2: category:blocks
  20: ci:wool
  21: ci:ironaxe

Categories:
  - ID: blocks
    Name: "&aBlocks"
    Icon: wool
    Description: "&7Browse building blocks"
    Items:
      - wool
      - EndStone
  • Size is a multiple of 9, up to 54. HeaderSize and FooterSize are the slots at the top and bottom that stay the same on every category page.
  • Slots keys start at 1 (key 1 is the first slot). Values:
    • ci:<item>: an item from items.yml
    • category:<id> (shop) or cat:<id> (upgrades): a button that opens a category
    • upg:<upgrade>: an upgrade, for example upg:sharpness
    • fill: the filler item, empty: nothing
  • Categories are the pages behind the category buttons: name, icon, description and the list of items shown on that page. The home category shows the default home page; players can change their own quick-buy slots.

Upgrades: protection, sharpness, haste, forge, healpool, dragonbuff, and the traps alarmtrap, blindtrap, miningfatiguetrap. Addons can add more.

Traps don't queue: when an enemy enters a base, every trap the team has bought fires at once and each loses one charge.

Which menu an arena uses: new arenas get DefaultTeamShopGui and DefaultTeamUpgradeGui from config.yml. In advanced setup mode, /bw setGui shop <guiId> and /bw setGui upgrade <guiId> choose another menu for one arena.

docs.title: Upgrade prices (upgrades.yml)
docs.text:
Every upgrade has a list of levels. The first entry is the price of level 1, the second of level 2 and so on, so the length of the list is the number of levels a team can buy:

DefaultCurrency: DIAMOND

Upgrades:
  SHARPNESS:
    - {price: 2, currency: DIAMOND}
    - {price: 4, currency: DIAMOND}
  HEALPOOL:
    - {price: 4, currency: DIAMOND}
  ALARMTRAP:
    - {price: 1, currency: DIAMOND}
    - {price: 2, currency: DIAMOND}
  • currency is IRON, GOLD, DIAMOND or EMERALD; when it is left out, DefaultCurrency is used.
  • A shorter list means fewer levels (up to what the upgrade supports). An empty list means the upgrade can't be bought.
  • Different prices for some arenas: an upgrade menu file can have its own UpgradePrices: section in the same format. Arenas that use that menu get those prices, for example cheaper upgrades in solo arenas. An entry that can not be read is logged once as a warning (naming the menu and the upgrade) and the prices from upgrades.yml are used for it. The built-in game modes each come with such a menu (upgradeSolo, upgradeDoubles, upgradeSquads, upgradeRush, upgradeDuels).
  • Different item prices for some arenas: a shop menu file can have an ItemPrices: section:
ItemPrices:
  IronSword: {price: 6, currency: GOLD}
  Wool: {price: 4, currency: IRON, amount: 32}

The keys are shop item ids from data/items.yml (not case-sensitive). price is required (0 to 100000), currency is optional (IRON, GOLD, DIAMOND or EMERALD; left out = the item's own), amount is optional (1 to 64; left out = the item's own). The prices apply to the menu in that file and, as a fallback, to any menu opened inside an arena whose shop menu has them. They change the /price/ and /amount/ text of the icon, the price that is charged and the amount that is given. An entry that can not be read is logged once and the item's own price is used. The web panel's shop menu editor can edit them.

docs.title: Generators (generators/*.yml)
docs.text:
Generators have no limit on how many items lie on the ground; items that nobody picks up stay until the game ends.

The built-in game modes each have a preset: generators/Solo.yml, Doubles.yml, Squads.yml, Rush.yml and Duels.yml (copied when missing). generators/defaultGenerators.yml is the old preset (deprecated, kept). A file sets how fast team, diamond and emerald generators drop resources at each level. Make another file with a different ConfigurationId for a faster or slower preset, and choose it with DefaultGeneratorConfig in config.yml (or Generators in a mode in modes.yml) or, per arena, /bw setGeneratorLeveling <configId> in advanced setup. The comments at the top of the file explain every value.

Diamond and emerald generators are upgraded by the game phases; team generators by the Forge upgrade.

ShowNextSpawnTime in each generator section turns the "next spawn in" countdown in the hologram above the generator on or off. By default it is on for diamond and emerald generators and off for team generators.

docs.title: Custom generators
docs.text:
A generator file can also define generators that drop any item, in a CustomGenerators section (there is a commented example at the end of defaultGenerators.yml):

CustomGenerators:
  gapple:
    Item: GOLDEN_APPLE
    Amount: 1
    SpawnDelay: 60
    Display: GOLD_BLOCK
    Name: "&6Golden Apple"
    ShowNextSpawnTime: true
Key Meaning Item What it drops Amount How many per drop (1 to 64, default 1) SpawnDelay Seconds between drops (default 30) Display The block that spins above it (default: the item) Name Title of its hologram, & colours allowed (default: the item name) ShowNextSpawnTime Show the countdown in the hologram (default true)

Place one in advanced setup mode with /bw setGenerator OTHER <id> [x y z], using the generator file of the arena (/bw setGeneratorLeveling). Custom generators have one level and are not upgraded by game phases. Like diamond and emerald generators, bridge eggs and portable towers don't build next to them.

docs.title: Player data storage: JSON or MySQL
docs.text:
NewBedwars keeps two kinds of player data:

  • Player data: language and quick-buy layout.
  • Stats: wins, losses, kills, deaths, final kills, beds broken and games played. Leaderboards and the stats placeholders use these.

Storage.Type in config.yml decides where they are kept:

Storage.Type Where Needs JSON (default) plugins/NewBedwars/data/playersData.json and playerStats.json Nothing MYSQL Tables nbw_player_data and nbw_player_stats in a MySQL/MariaDB database A database and the MySQL: section in config.yml

Arenas, groups, GUIs and other settings always stay in files. Only player data and stats move to the database.

docs.title: Do I need MySQL?
docs.text:
On one server: no. No feature or gameplay change needs it, and JSON is the simplest choice: nothing to install, and the data sits in the plugin folder.

MySQL is still worth it on a single server when:

  1. You want stats outside Minecraft. A website leaderboard, a Discord bot or a stats page can read nbw_player_stats directly instead of parsing a JSON file in the server folder.
  2. Several separate servers should share stats. Servers that are not a NewBedwars network (no Velocity proxy) but use the same database share stats, leaderboards and player settings.
  3. You have many players. With JSON, all stats are held in memory and the whole file is rewritten on save. With MySQL, a player's row is loaded when they join, and a game result only adds to their numbers.
  4. You want database tools. You can make dumps and scheduled backups, or fix one player's stats with a query while the server is running.

On a Velocity network: use MYSQL on every server if stats and leaderboards should be the same everywhere. Without it, each server counts its own stats. Network mode has one more optional database feature, the server status table. See network.md.

docs.title: Switching to MySQL
docs.text:
1. Create a database and a user for it (MySQL or MariaDB).
  2. Fill in the MySQL: section of config.yml (Host, Port, Database, User, Password) and set Storage.Type: MYSQL.
  3. Restart the server. The tables are created automatically. On the first start with an empty database, the server's JSON data is imported once. The JSON files are left in place, but they are no longer updated.

The plugin uses the MySQL driver that ships with the server, so nothing else needs to be installed.

For a database on another machine, set MySQL.SslMode: REQUIRED (or VERIFY_CA / VERIFY_IDENTITY with a trusted certificate). The default PREFERRED encrypts only when the database offers it and does not check the certificate.

docs.title: Tables
docs.text:
Table Columns nbw_player_data uuid (key), name, language, fast_buy, updated nbw_player_stats uuid (key), name, wins, losses, kills, deaths, final_kills, beds_broken, games_played

Rows are keyed by the player's UUID, so a player who changes their Minecraft name keeps their stats; name is the last name the player joined with. Reading these tables from other programs is safe. The plugin only ever adds to stats (wins = wins + 1) and never overwrites them, so editing a stat by hand is safe too. An online player sees the new value after they rejoin.

docs.title: Upgrading from 2.6-beta or older
docs.text:
Before 2.7-beta, player data and stats were stored by player name (tables nbw_players and nbw_stats, and name keys in the JSON files). On the first start of 2.7-beta:

  • JSON: playerStats.json is rewritten with UUID keys; the old file is kept as playerStats.json.before-uuid. playersData.json is rewritten with UUID keys on the next save.
  • MySQL: when the new tables are empty, the rows of nbw_players and nbw_stats are copied into nbw_player_data and nbw_player_stats. The old tables are left untouched as a backup and can be dropped once everything looks right. Programs that read nbw_stats (website leaderboards, bots) must switch to nbw_player_stats.

Stats of a name with no known UUID (a player who never joined since player data was saved) get the offline-mode UUID of that name. Stats that were split between an old and a new name of the same player are added together.

docs.title: Getting started
docs.text:
Everything in the com.l299l.newbedwars.api package and its subpackages (view, edit, command, registry, events, game, maintenance, shop, mode, tablist, scoreboard, bossbar, text) is the stable contract for addons. All other packages are internal and can change in any update.

Important

New in 2.8-beta:

  • API version: NewBedwarsAPI.getApiVersion(), and the compatibility rules for the stable releases.
  • Shop items: ShopItem has commands, openGui, givePermission and priceMaterial for the new COMMANDS, OPEN_GUI and GIVE_PERM actions and priceType OTHER (the 12-argument constructor still works).
  • ShopGui.closeOnTransaction and CommandContext.SETUP_BUILDING are marked for removal in 3.0.0.
  • Players: join, spectate, leave and sendToLobby with a JoinResult.
  • Parties: getParty(Player) (PartyView) and PartyChangeEvent.
  • Messages and languages: getLanguage, getMessage and registerMessages for translated addon texts.
  • Statistics: getStats(UUID), loadStats(UUID) and addStat to count stats for addon game modes.
  • Game modes: getModes() (ModeService) lists the modes and phase lists of modes.yml and applies a mode to a waiting arena; ArenaView.getGeneratorConfig() and getGamePhases().
  • Game control: destroyBed, eliminateTeam and setUpgradeLevel.
  • Display: custom placeholders, tab lists (TablistService, TablistUpdateEvent), scoreboards (ScoreboardService, ScoreboardUpdateEvent) and boss bars (BossBarService, BossBarUpdateEvent).
  • Game modes can also be created and saved through the API (saveMode and related methods).
  • TeamPickEvent: fired when a player picks a team in the waiting lobby (cancellable).
  • New events: ArenaStateChangeEvent (also the countdown start and cancel), TeamsAssignedEvent, PlayerRespawnArenaEvent, PlayerSpectateEvent, TrapTriggerEvent, PartyChangeEvent. ShopPurchaseEvent has getTeam() and setPrice(int); BedBreakEvent.getBreaker() is null when the bed was destroyed through destroyBed.
  • Custom generators: GeneratorKind.CUSTOM, GeneratorView.getCustomId(), ArenaView.getCustomGeneratorIds() and ArenaEditor.addCustomGenerator(id, location). Before, custom generators were reported as BASIC.
  • Team display names: TeamEditor.setDisplayName / TeamView.getDisplayName() change the name players see (e.g. Lime for a team Red that got a lime color) without renaming the team.
  • ShopItemStackEvent: change or replace the item stack of a shop item per player, both the menu icon and the item the player gets.
  • ArenaView.getMaxPlayers(), getTeam(Player) and isSpectator(Player); ShopLogic.perform(player, arena, itemName) tells the logic which shop item was used.

Pages of the addon API documentation:

  • Reading data and events: reading data, events, extra data
  • Registering your own content: phase actions, shop item logic, shop items, armor tiers, upgrades and traps, subcommands
  • Arenas: editing arenas, arena maintenance, game control
  • Players: join, spectate and leave, parties, statistics and leaderboards, messages and languages
  • Display: placeholders, tab list, scoreboards, boss bars
  • Shop editor and game modes
  • Full example

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text:
From the first stable release (3.0.0) NewBedwars uses MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH version numbers, and the API follows these rules:

Release Example What can change in the API Patch 3.0.0 → 3.0.1 Nothing. Bug fixes only Minor 3.0 → 3.1 Only additions: new methods, events, enum values, registries, record components (the old record constructor is kept). An addon built for 3.0 keeps working on every 3.x Major 3.x → 4.0 Members that were deprecated may be removed
  • Deprecation first. Anything that will be removed is marked @Deprecated(forRemoval = true) (your compiler warns about it), its javadoc names the replacement, and it stays for at least one minor release. It is removed only in the next major version.
  • Interfaces you implement (AddonCommand, ShopLogic, PhaseActionHandler, UpgradeDefinition.Effect) only get new methods with a default implementation. All other interfaces (ArenaView, ShopEditor, ...) are implemented by NewBedwars and can get new methods in any minor release, so don't implement them yourself.
  • Enums can get new values in a minor release (for example a new CommandContext or StatType). Give every switch over an API enum a default branch.
  • Not covered: everything outside com.l299l.newbedwars.api, and behaviour that a bug fix corrects.
  • Before 3.0.0 (the 2.x-beta versions) the API could still change between releases. Two deprecated members will be removed in 3.0.0: ShopGui.closeOnTransaction (always false) and CommandContext.SETUP_BUILDING (use SETUP_AUTOMATIC).

docs.title: API version
docs.text:
api.getApiVersion() returns a number that goes up by one in every release that adds something to the API. Check it to find out whether a feature exists on the server your addon runs on:

if (api.getApiVersion() >= 1) {
    // 2.8-beta or newer: ShopItem.commands(), getApiVersion(), ...
}
API version NewBedwars 1 2.8-beta

getApiVersion() itself exists from 2.8-beta. To support older versions, catch NoSuchMethodError or compare api.getVersion().

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
Add the dependency from JitPack with provided scope:

<repositories>
    <repository>
        <id>jitpack.io</id>
        <url>https://jitpack.io</url>
    </repository>
</repositories>

<dependencies>
    <dependency>
        <groupId>com.github.l299l.NewBedwars-Free</groupId>
        <artifactId>newbedwars-api</artifactId>
        <version>v2.8-beta</version>
        <scope>provided</scope>
    </dependency>
</dependencies>

Then depend on the plugin in plugin.yml:

name: MyAddon
main: com.example.MyAddon
version: 1.0
api-version: "1.17"
depend: [NewBedwars]

Get the API in onEnable (it throws IllegalStateException when NewBedwars is not enabled). It is also registered in Bukkit's ServicesManager:

NewBedwarsAPI api = NewBedwarsAPI.get();
// or: Bukkit.getServicesManager().load(NewBedwarsAPI.class)

docs.title: Rules and good practice
docs.text:
• Call the API from the main thread (join, spectate, leave, sendToLobby, addStat and registerShopItem throw IllegalStateException on another thread). Exceptions that may be called from any thread: getMaintenance(), getGameControl() and getShop() (the work runs on the main thread, the futures complete there), and the stats futures getLeaderboard, loadStats and findPlayers (with MySQL they complete on a database thread, so switch to the main thread before using Bukkit).
  • Events fire on the main thread; keep handlers fast.
  • Do not teleport players to the lobby yourself: NewBedwars does it through PlayerSendToLobbyEvent, so network setups keep working.
  • Do not hold on to worlds from ArenaView#getWorld(); fetch it again after ArenaResetEvent stage POST.
  • Registrations are tied to your plugin; no cleanup code is needed on disable.

docs.title: Arenas
docs.text: See Getting started for how to get NewBedwarsAPI api and the dependency.

docs.title: Editing arenas
docs.text:
api.edit(arena) returns an ArenaEditor. It only works while the arena is WAITING (otherwise IllegalStateException); invalid input throws IllegalArgumentException. Locations must be in the arena world. Changes are saved shortly after, or call save().

ArenaEditor editor = api.edit(arena);
editor.setMinPlayers(2);
TeamEditor red = editor.createTeam("Red", ChatColor.RED);
red.setSpawn(spawnLoc);
red.setBed(bedLoc);                          // a bed must be placed there
red.setShop(shopLoc, EntityType.VILLAGER);
red.setUpgrades(upgLoc, EntityType.VILLAGER);
red.setGenerator(genLoc);
editor.addGenerator(GeneratorKind.DIAMOND, diamondLoc);
editor.addCustomGenerator("gapple", appleLoc); // an id from ArenaView#getCustomGeneratorIds() (2.8-beta)
editor.removeGenerator(0);                   // index in ArenaView#getGenerators()
editor.removeTeam("Blue");

ArenaEditor: setMinPlayers, setMaxInTeam, setWaitingSpawn, createTeam, getTeam, removeTeam, addGenerator (DIAMOND/EMERALD), addCustomGenerator(id, location) (2.8-beta) (IllegalArgumentException when the arena's generator file has no such id), removeGenerator, setShopGui(guiId) / setUpgradeGui(guiId) (the GUI of data/guis/ the shop and upgrade NPCs of the arena open), save. TeamEditor: setColor, setDisplayName (2.8-beta) (1 to 32 characters without colour codes or line breaks, null = show the name again; saved with the arena), setSpawn, setBed/clearBed, setShop/clearShop, setUpgrades/clearUpgrades, setGenerator/clearGenerator.

docs.title: Team colors and display names (2.8-beta)
docs.text:
A team keeps the name it was created with (getName()): the arena file, commands and upgrades use it. When your addon gives teams other colors, set a display name too, so players don't see a lime team called "Red". Chat, titles, the scoreboard, NPC names and %newbedwars_team% show the display name.

TeamEditor red = api.edit(arena).getTeam("Red").orElseThrow();
red.setColor(ChatColor.GREEN);
red.setDisplayName("Lime");

docs.title: Changing shop items per player (2.8-beta)
docs.text:
ShopItemStackEvent lets you change what a shop item shows and gives, per player. It fires for the menu icon (Use.ICON) and for the item the player gets (Use.GIVEN), so both match. Keep the item meta when you replace the stack: it holds the name, the description and the key NewBedwars uses to recognise its items.

@EventHandler
public void onShopItem(ShopItemStackEvent e) {
    if (!e.getItemName().equals("Wood")) return;
    if (e.getTeam().map(t -> t.getColor() == ChatColor.RED).orElse(false)) {
        ItemStack planks = new ItemStack(Material.MANGROVE_PLANKS, e.getItem().getAmount());
        planks.setItemMeta(e.getItem().getItemMeta());
        e.setItem(planks);
    }
}

Wool, glass, terracotta and the other team-colored blocks are already in the team color.

docs.title: Arena maintenance
docs.text:
api.getMaintenance() returns ArenaMaintenance, the arena actions of /bw arena for addons such as a web panel. The same checks as the commands apply (e.g. nothing is changed while players are in the arena).

Method Does enable(arena) / disable(arena) like /bw arena enable/disable (disable sends waiting players out) backup(arena) saves the arena file and map; detail() is the backup id listBackups(arena) List<ArenaBackup> (id, hasArenaFile, hasMap), newest first restore(arena, backupId) restores file and map; backupId null = newest export(arena) zip with arena file + map in getExportFolder(); detail() is its path importArena(fileName) loads a zip from getExportFolder(); the new arena is disabled copy(arena, newName) copy with settings and map, joins the same group resetMap(arena) puts the map back to its saved state (completes when the reset started) delete(arena) deletes the arena file, world and saved map (backups are kept) getExportFolder() plugins/NewBedwars/data/exports

Every action returns a CompletableFuture<MaintenanceResult>. The methods can be called from any thread: the work runs on the server thread (file copying in the background) and the future completes on the server thread. A refused action is a normal result, not an exception:

api.getMaintenance().backup("castle").thenAccept(result -> {
    if (result.isSuccess()) getLogger().info("Backup " + result.detail());
    else getLogger().warning(result.code() + ": " + result.message());
});

MaintenanceResult: code() (OK, NOT_FOUND, BUSY, ALREADY_DONE, NOT_READY, INVALID_NAME, NAME_TAKEN, UNAVAILABLE on a LOBBY server, FAILED, PARTIAL = deleted but some files remain), isSuccess(), arena(), message() (the command's message in the server's default language, without colors) and detail() (backup id, export file, copy source or error text; may be null). listBackups completes exceptionally with NoSuchElementException for an unknown arena.

docs.title: Game control
docs.text:
api.getGameControl() returns GameControl, the actions of /bw game without a player in the arena. actor is the name players see in the messages (e.g. "Panel: Alex").

Method Does Refused (NOT_READY) when start(arena, actor) starts the countdown the arena is not waiting forceStart(arena, actor) starts the game now the arena is not waiting or starting stop(arena, actor) ends the game as a draw (stats saved) no game runs forceStop(arena, actor) stops and resets the arena at once never nextPhase(arena, actor) skips to the next game phase no game runs broadcast(arena, actor, message) sends message (& colours, 1 to 256 characters, INVALID_NAME otherwise) to all players and spectators of the arena destroyBed(arena, team, actor) (2.8-beta) destroys the team's bed as if an enemy broke it (BedBreakEvent with a null breaker, can be cancelled: FAILED); ALREADY_DONE when the bed is gone no game runs eliminateTeam(arena, team, actor) (2.8-beta) destroys the bed, makes the team's players spectators and runs the win check (the game ends when one team is left); ALREADY_DONE when the team is out no game runs setUpgradeLevel(arena, team, upgrade, level, actor) (2.8-beta) sets a team upgrade or the number of a trap for free; raising applies each level like a purchase, only traps can be lowered (INVALID_NAME otherwise and for a level above the upgrade's maximum, NOT_FOUND for an unknown upgrade). TeamUpgradeEvent is not fired no game runs

Team names are matched without case; an unknown team is NOT_FOUND. All return CompletableFuture<MaintenanceResult> like arena maintenance (NOT_FOUND for an unknown arena), can be called from any thread and run on the server thread.

docs.title: Reading data and events
docs.text: See Getting started for how to get NewBedwarsAPI api and the dependency.

docs.title: Reading data
docs.text:
NewBedwarsAPI hands out read-only views. Views stay valid while the arena exists, but never keep ArenaView#getWorld(): the world is replaced after every map reset.

Method Returns getVersion() plugin version getApiVersion() (2.8-beta) the API version, a number getArenas() all arenas getArena(String name) / getArena(World) / getArena(Player) Optional<ArenaView> (the player variant also finds spectators) getGroups() / getGroup(String name) (2.6-beta) arena groups (maps voted between), Optional<ArenaGroupView> getSetupArena(Player) / getSetupPlayers() (2.7-beta) the arena a player is setting up (in setup mode), Optional<ArenaView>; everyone in setup mode as Map<Player, ArenaView> getNetworkMode() (2.6-beta) NONE, GAME or LOBBY (Network.Mode) getNetworkArenas() (2.6-beta) on LOBBY and GAME servers: the arenas of all game servers (NetworkArenaView: server, name, group, state, players, isJoinable(), getFreeSlots()), empty otherwise getServerId() (2.6-beta) this server's name in the proxy, empty when not in network mode getNetworkRejoin(Player) (2.6-beta) on a LOBBY server: the network arena the player can still rejoin getStats(String name) (2.6-beta) / getStats(UUID) (2.8-beta) PlayerStatsView (wins, losses, kills, deaths, final kills, beds, games; zeros when unknown). With MySQL storage these are network-wide; only online/loaded players are known. The UUID variant still finds a player who changed their name getParty(Player) (2.8-beta) Optional<PartyView>, see Parties getLanguage(Player) / getMessage(Player, key) (2.8-beta) the player's language code and a translated message, see Messages and languages

ArenaView: getName, getState (ArenaState), isEnabled, getWorld, getMinPlayers, getMaxInTeam, getPlayers, getSpectators, getTeams, getTeam(name), getGamePlayer(UUID), getCurrentPhase, getGameTime (seconds), getNextPhase / getPhaseTimeLeft (NEW in 2.7-beta) (next phase name or null; seconds left in the current phase, -1 when none), getGenerators, getExtra(Plugin), getShopGui / getUpgradeGui (ids of the GUIs the arena's shop and upgrade NPCs open), getLoadProblems (NEW in 2.7-beta) (why the arena was loaded disabled; empty when it loaded fine), getQuickVoidY / getSetupPlayers (NEW in 2.7-beta) (the quick void level, null while not set; online players who are setting the arena up), getMaxPlayers / getTeam(Player) / isSpectator(Player) / getCustomGeneratorIds (NEW in 2.8-beta) (teams times team size; the team of a player, empty before the teams are assigned; whether the player watches, is out or waits for a respawn; the ids from CustomGenerators in the arena's generator file).

TeamView: getName (never changes; identifies the team), getDisplayName (2.8-beta) (what players see: the display name or getName), getColor, getPlayers, isAlive, isBedDestroyed, getSpawn (may be null), getBed (NEW in 2.7-beta, may be null), getUpgradeLevel(String upgrade), getExtra(Plugin).

ArenaGroupView (2.6-beta): getName, getArenaNames (as configured, may include missing arenas), getArenas (existing ones), getDisplayItem, getProblems (missing arenas, different team sizes).

GamePlayerView: getPlayer, getTeam (empty while the arena is waiting; teams are assigned at game start), getKills, getFinalKills, getDeaths, getBedsBroken.

GeneratorView: getKind (GeneratorKind: BASIC, DIAMOND, EMERALD, CUSTOM (2.8-beta)), getLocation, getCustomId (2.8-beta) (the CustomGenerators id of a CUSTOM generator, null otherwise).

PartyView (2.8-beta): getLeader, getMembers (UUIDs, online or not), getOnlineMembers, contains(UUID), size.

docs.title: Events
docs.text:
Normal Bukkit events: register a Listener as usual. All arena events extend ArenaEvent#getArena().

Event Cancellable Fired Useful getters GameStartEvent no game starts, teams assigned GameEndEvent no game ends, before the winner announcement getWinner() (null = draw) ArenaResetEvent no before (PRE) and after (POST) a map reset getStage() PlayerJoinArenaEvent yes before a player joins or rejoins getPlayer(), isRejoin() PlayerLeaveArenaEvent no a player or spectator leaves getPlayer(), getReason() (LeaveReason: COMMAND, DISCONNECT, KICKED, OTHER) BedBreakEvent yes before an enemy bed breaks, or GameControl#destroyBed destroys it getTeam(), getBreaker() (null for destroyBed) PlayerKillEvent no a player dies in a running game getVictim(), getKiller() (nullable), isFinalKill(), getCause() (VOID for every void death), getDragonTeam() (the team whose dragon killed the victim) ShopPurchaseEvent yes before a purchase is charged (only when the player can pay the normal price) getPlayer(), getItemName(), getKind() (ITEM, ARMOR, TOOL, UPGRADE), getPriceType() (the material for priceType: OTHER), getPrice(), setPrice(int) (2.8-beta) (0 = free, never negative), getTeam() (2.8-beta) TeamUpgradeEvent yes before an upgrade or trap is bought getTeam(), getUpgrade(), getNewLevel(), getBuyer() ArmorEquipEvent no before armor is applied (respawn, purchase) getPlayer(), getArmor(), setArmor(ItemStack[]) (boots, leggings, chestplate, helmet) MapVoteEvent (2.6-beta) yes during the after-game time, a player of the ended arena votes for the next map getPlayer(), getVotedArena() (null when the arena is on another game server), getVotedNetworkArena() MapChosenEvent (2.6-beta) no the after-game time is over and a next map won; the arena then stops and everyone joins the chosen arena getGroup(), getChosenArena() (null when on another game server), getChosenNetworkArena() GamePhaseChangeEvent (2.7-beta) no the game moves to the next phase (also the first phase at game start) getPrevious() (null at the first phase), getNext(), isForced() (admin skipped) ArenaChatEvent (2.7-beta) no after a player's arena or team chat message was delivered getPlayer(), getMessage() (without colours), isTeamChat(), getTeam() (nullable) BedsDestroyedEvent (2.7-beta) no the bed destruction phase destroyed the remaining beds getTeams() TeamEliminatedEvent (2.7-beta) no a team is out (no bed, no living players) getTeam() GeneratorUpgradeEvent (2.7-beta) no a game phase upgraded the diamond or emerald generators getKind(), getLevel() ArenaStateChangeEvent (2.8-beta) no after the arena state changed: WAITING→STARTING countdown started, STARTING→WAITING countdown cancelled, →PLAYING game started, PLAYING→ENDING, ENDING→RESTARTING→WAITING map reset; disabling = RESTARTING, enabling = WAITING getPrevious(), getNext() TeamsAssignedEvent (2.8-beta) no at the game start, after every player got a team and before the teleport to the team spawns and GameStartEvent (read the teams from getArena()) PlayerRespawnArenaEvent (2.8-beta) no a player respawned at their team spawn, with armor, items and upgrades given back getPlayer(), getTeam() PlayerSpectateEvent (2.8-beta) yes before a player who doesn't play starts spectating (/bw spectate, the menu, api.spectate); not for dead or eliminated players getPlayer() TrapTriggerEvent (2.8-beta) yes before one trap of a team goes off (one event per trap); cancelled = the trap is kept and does nothing getTeam() (the owner), getEnemy(), getTrap() (upgrade name) ShopItemStackEvent (2.8-beta) no NewBedwars built the stack of a shop item for one player: a menu icon (ICON, shop, upgrades, quick-buy editor) or the item the player gets (GIVEN, also permanent items after a respawn); not an ArenaEvent getPlayer(), getItemName(), getUse(), getItem() / setItem(ItemStack), getArena(), getTeam() (both Optional) PartyChangeEvent (2.8-beta) no after a party on this server changed (not for changes synced from the proxy; not an ArenaEvent) getParty(), getPlayer() (null for DISBANDED), getChange() (CREATED, JOINED, LEFT, KICKED, LEADER_CHANGED, DISBANDED) TeamPickEvent (2.8-beta) yes before a player's pick in the waiting lobby is stored (team selector item or /bw team); cancelled = the old pick is kept getPlayer(), getTeam() (Optional<TeamView>, empty = pick cleared / random), getPreviousTeam() (Optional<TeamView>), getMovedPlayers() (the whole party when the leader picks) TablistUpdateEvent (2.8-beta) yes just before a changed tab list (header, footer or list name) is sent to a player; not fired while nothing changed; cancelled = nothing is sent for this change; not an ArenaEvent getPlayer(), getArena() (Optional, empty in the lobby), getLayout() (null in the lobby), getHeader() / setHeader(String), getFooter() / setFooter(String), getPlayerListName() / setPlayerListName(String) ScoreboardUpdateEvent (2.8-beta) yes just before a changed sidebar scoreboard (title or lines) is sent to a player; not fired while nothing changed; cancelled = nothing is sent for this change; not an ArenaEvent getPlayer(), getArena() (Optional), getScoreboard() (id), getTitle() / setTitle(String), getLines() (a copy) / setLines(List<String>) (at most 15 lines) BossBarUpdateEvent (2.8-beta) yes when a boss bar of bossBars.yml switches to a new text (a step of its Texts cycle, or an arena starts showing it at a phase change); not for addon boss bars; cancelled = the previous display is kept for this step (the first display is shown as configured); not an ArenaEvent getArena() (Optional, empty for MainLobby), getBossBar() (id), getText() / setText(String), getColor() / setColor(BarColor), getStyle() / setStyle(BarStyle) PlayerSendToLobbyEvent yes whenever a player is sent to the lobby getPlayer(), getReason() (ADDON for api.sendToLobby, from 2.8-beta), getTarget()/setTarget() NetworkJoinRequestEvent (2.6-beta) yes on a LOBBY server, before a join or rejoin request goes to the proxy (/bw join, NPCs, selector, /bw rejoin, API); cancelled = nothing is sent and NewBedwars sends no message getPlayer(), getKind() (ANY, GROUP, ARENA, REJOIN, SPECTATE), getTarget() NetworkArenasUpdateEvent (2.6-beta) no on a LOBBY server, when the network arena list changed (not an ArenaEvent) getArenas()

PlayerSendToLobbyEvent is the hook for custom networks: cancel it and send the player to a lobby server yourself (the built-in network mode already does this on GAME servers). Reasons: LEFT_ARENA, LOBBY_COMMAND, JOINED_IN_ARENA_WORLD, MAP_RESET, ARENA_UNLOADED, ARENA_DELETED, SETUP_ENDED, SERVER_SHUTDOWN, RELOAD.

docs.title: Network actions (LOBBY servers) (2.6-beta)
docs.text:
NewBedwarsAPI api = NewBedwarsAPI.get();
if (api.getNetworkMode() == NetworkMode.LOBBY) {
    // Same checks and messages as /bw join: permission, only the party admin, ...
    api.requestNetworkJoin(player, "solo");      // group, arena name, or null for any arena
    api.getNetworkRejoin(player).ifPresent(a -> api.requestNetworkRejoin(player));
}

Both return false when this is not a lobby server, a check failed, a NetworkJoinRequestEvent listener cancelled it, or the proxy can not be reached.

docs.title: Extra data
docs.text:
Store your own settings inside an arena or team. They are saved in the arena file and never touched by NewBedwars. Each addon has its own namespace (its plugin name).

ExtraData data = arena.getExtra(this);
data.set("difficulty", 3);
int d = data.getInt("difficulty", 1);

Getters take a default; setters exist for String, int, double, boolean; also has, remove, keys. Changes are written to disk shortly after (no manual save).

docs.title: Display
docs.text: See Getting started for how to get NewBedwarsAPI api and the dependency.

docs.title: Placeholders
docs.text:
Important

New in 2.8-beta.

api.registerPlaceholder(owner, name, placeholder) adds one custom placeholder that works everywhere NewBedwars renders text: {name} in tablists.yml, and /name/ in scoreboards.yml, bossBars.yml and the boss bars of addons (BossBarService#show).

api.registerPlaceholder(this, "rank", (viewer, arena) -> ranks.of(viewer));

TextPlaceholder#resolve(Player viewer, ArenaView arenaOrNull) is called on the server thread every time a text using it is rendered, so keep it fast. viewer is the player the text is for (in a tab list PlayerFormat the player being listed). It is null for the boss bars of an arena and the lobby boss bar, because all players of the arena share one bar. The arena is null outside arenas. & colours in the result are translated afterwards; null counts as empty.

A name is 1 to 32 letters, digits or _. registerPlaceholder throws IllegalArgumentException for other names, for names any of the three systems uses itself (compared ignoring case, e.g. player, arena, teamColor, map, status, arena_name) and for names that are already registered. An exception thrown by your placeholder is logged once per name and renders as empty text. Placeholders are removed when your plugin is disabled or on unregisterAll(owner); they also survive /bw reload. Scoreboards do not apply PlaceholderAPI.

The tab list has a shortcut, api.getTablists().registerPlaceholder, that adds {name} for the tab list only:

api.getTablists().registerPlaceholder(this, "rank", (viewer, arena) -> ranks.of(viewer));

TablistPlaceholder has the same resolve(Player viewer, ArenaView arenaOrNull) as TextPlaceholder. In the PlayerFormat of a tab list the player is the one whose name is being listed, and the arena is null in the lobby.

docs.title: Tab list
docs.text:
Important

New in 2.8-beta.

api.getTablists() returns TablistService, a view of the custom tab list (tablists.yml). Call it on the server thread.

Method Returns / does isEnabled() Tablist.Enabled from config.yml getLayouts() ids of the layouts in tablists.yml, sorted getDefaultLayout() DefaultTablist from config.yml getEffectiveLayout(arena) the layout an arena's players get: the arena's own (ArenaView#getTablist()), else the default, and Default when that layout doesn't exist. null gives the default isLobbyEnabled() whether players outside arenas get the Lobby tab list registerPlaceholder(owner, name, placeholder) adds {name} for the Header, Footer and PlayerFormat lines setPlayerLayout(player, layoutId) / clearPlayerLayout(player) a layout for one player refresh(player) / refresh(arena) renders now instead of at the next 1 second tick

Custom placeholders for the tab list: see Placeholders above.

docs.title: Layouts per player
docs.text: setPlayerLayout(player, "Fancy") makes the player see that layout instead of the arena's or the default one. It applies inside arenas only and is removed when the player leaves the arena, quits, or you call clearPlayerLayout(player); it survives /bw reload. An unknown layout id throws IllegalArgumentException.

docs.title: Arena layout and modes
docs.text: ArenaView#getTablist() is the layout id set on the arena (/bw setTablist), null = server default. ArenaEditor#setTablist(layoutId) changes it while the arena is waiting (null = default, an unknown id throws IllegalArgumentException); like the other setters it is saved with save() and it refreshes the tab list of the arena's players. Game modes carry it as ModeInfo#tablist (see Game modes).

docs.title: Changing what is sent
docs.text:
TablistUpdateEvent is fired just before a changed header, footer or list name is sent to a player. It is not fired while the rendered tab list is unchanged, so it never runs every tick. Set the texts you want with setHeader, setFooter and setPlayerListName (null header/footer count as empty, a null list name shows the vanilla name), or cancel it to send nothing for this change. What your listener decides is only asked again when the rendered tab list changes or after refresh, so keep the result a function of the event's values or call refresh when your data changes.

@EventHandler
public void onTablist(TablistUpdateEvent e) {
    e.setFooter(e.getFooter() + "\n&7Play on " + host);
}

docs.title: Scoreboards
docs.text:
Important

New in 2.8-beta.

api.getScoreboards() returns ScoreboardService, a view of the sidebar scoreboards of scoreboards.yml. Call it on the server thread.

Method Returns / does getScoreboards() ids in scoreboards.yml, sorted isEnabled(id) whether the scoreboard exists and has Enabled: true getCurrentScoreboard(player) the id shown to the player now, null outside arenas, when hidden or disabled setPlayerScoreboard(player, id) / clearPlayerScoreboard(player) a scoreboard for one player instead of the one the arena state picks; an unknown id throws IllegalArgumentException hide(player) / show(player) removes the NewBedwars sidebar for the player (for addons that draw their own), or brings it back refresh(player) renders now instead of at the next 1 second tick

The override and hide apply inside arenas only and are removed when the player leaves the arena or quits (hide also when you call show). An override for a scoreboard with Enabled: false shows nothing.

ScoreboardUpdateEvent is fired just before a changed title or lines are sent to a player. It is not fired while the rendered scoreboard is unchanged, so it never runs every tick. Set what you want with setTitle and setLines (at most 15 lines, otherwise IllegalArgumentException; equal lines are made unique automatically), or cancel it to send nothing for this change. A title you change replaces the animated TitleEffect. What your listener decides is only asked again when the rendered scoreboard changes or after refresh, so keep the result a function of the event's values or call refresh when your data changes.

@EventHandler
public void onScoreboard(ScoreboardUpdateEvent e) {
    List<String> lines = e.getLines();
    if (lines.size() < 15) lines.add("&7" + host);
    e.setLines(lines);
}

docs.title: Boss bars
docs.text:
Important

New in 2.8-beta.

api.getBossBars() returns BossBarService. Call it on the server thread.

Method Returns / does getBossBars() ids in bossBars.yml, sorted isEnabled(id) whether the boss bar exists and has Enabled: true show(owner, player, text, color, style, progress) shows your own boss bar to one player and returns an AddonBossBar 
AddonBossBar bar = api.getBossBars().show(this, player, "&eEvent in /players/ players", BarColor.YELLOW, BarStyle.SOLID, 1.0);
bar.setProgress(0.5);
bar.remove();

The text supports & colours, the /name/ placeholders of bossBars.yml, placeholders registered with registerPlaceholder and PlaceholderAPI when it is installed; a text with placeholders is resolved again every second. AddonBossBar has getPlayer(), setText, setColor, setStyle, setProgress (clamped to 0..1), isVisible() and remove(). A bar is removed when the player quits, leaves or changes the arena (if it was shown while the player was in one), when your plugin is disabled, on unregisterAll(owner) and when NewBedwars is disabled; isVisible() is then false.

BossBarUpdateEvent is fired when a boss bar of bossBars.yml switches to a new text (a step of its Texts cycle, or an arena starts showing it at a phase change), not for addon boss bars.
