Change setText, setColor and setStyle, or cancel it to keep the previous display for this step. A text you change is no longer refreshed every second until the next step. For arena boss bars the placeholders are resolved without a viewer (all players of the arena share the bar).

docs.title: Full example
docs.text: This page walks through a complete addon, docs/examples/event-logger. Every snippet below is copied from its source, EventLoggerPlugin.java, so you can find it there. The other pages explain each API in detail; this one shows them working together.

docs.title: What the addon does
docs.text:
• Logs every API event to the console and to the chat of players with nbwlogger.use.
  • Registers a phase action (NBWLOG), shop item logic (NBWLIGHTNING), an armor tier (NBWTEST), a team upgrade (NBWSPEED), a trap (NBWBLIND) and one subcommand (/bw nbwinfo).
  • Stores its own data in arenas and teams (extra data) and edits an arena with the arena editor.
  • Adds a placeholder logger_events, an addon boss bar, a scoreboard line and a tab list footer line.
  • Adds /nbwlog (chat, modes, edit) to print what the read-only API sees.

To build it, run mvn package in the example folder (the NewBedwars API comes from JitPack) and copy target/NewBedwarsEventLogger-1.0.jar into the server's plugins/ folder next to NewBedwars. It needs NewBedwars 2.8-beta or newer.

docs.title: Project setup
docs.text:
pom.xml: the JitPack repository and the API as a provided dependency, because NewBedwars supplies the classes at runtime. Never shade the API into your jar. The example compiles against Paper 1.17.1, the oldest supported version; see Getting started.

    <repositories>
        <repository>
            <id>papermc-repo</id>
            <url>https://repo.papermc.io/repository/maven-public/</url>
        </repository>
        <repository>
            <id>jitpack.io</id>
            <url>https://jitpack.io</url>
        </repository>
    </repositories>

        <dependency>
            <groupId>com.github.l299l.NewBedwars-Free</groupId>
            <artifactId>newbedwars-api</artifactId>
            <version>v2.8-beta</version>
            <scope>provided</scope>
        </dependency>

plugin.yml has to list NewBedwars in depend, so it loads first and its API service exists when your onEnable runs:

name: NewBedwarsEventLogger
version: 1.0
main: com.example.nbwlogger.EventLoggerPlugin
api-version: "1.17"
depend: [NewBedwars]
description: Logs every NewBedwars API event for testing.
commands:
  nbwlog:
    description: "NewBedwarsEventLogger: /nbwlog [chat|modes|edit]"
    usage: /nbwlog [chat|modes|edit]
    permission: nbwlogger.use
permissions:
  nbwlogger.use:
    default: op

docs.title: Getting the API
docs.text:
NewBedwarsAPI.get() returns the API, and throws when NewBedwars is not enabled. The addon also checks the API version: the display features need API version 1 (2.8-beta), so on anything older it disables itself instead of failing later. getApiVersion() itself exists from 2.8-beta; to support older servers too, catch NoSuchMethodError as described in Getting started.

    @Override
    public void onEnable() {
        Bukkit.getPluginManager().registerEvents(this, this);
        NewBedwarsAPI api = NewBedwarsAPI.get();
        getLogger().info("API version of NewBedwars: " + api.getVersion());
        if (api.getApiVersion() < 1) {
            getLogger().warning("NewBedwars 2.8-beta or newer is needed for the display APIs, disabling.");
            getServer().getPluginManager().disablePlugin(this);
            return;
        }
        registerAll(api);
    }

docs.title: Listening to events
docs.text:
NewBedwars events are normal Bukkit events, so the addon is a Listener and registers itself on the first line of onEnable. Most handlers only read data and use EventPriority.MONITOR, which runs after other plugins have decided and sees the final result:

    @EventHandler(priority = EventPriority.MONITOR)
    public void onKill(PlayerKillEvent e) {
        String killer = e.getKiller() == null ? "none" : e.getKiller().getName();
        log("Kill victim=" + e.getVictim().getName() + " killer=" + killer + " final=" + e.isFinalKill() + " cause=" + e.getCause());
    }

Events that can be cancelled are handled earlier, at the default priority. The example has a CANCEL_TEST switch for trying that: with it set to true, bed breaks of the team "Red" and purchases of "Wool" are cancelled.

    @EventHandler
    public void onBed(BedBreakEvent e) {
        if (CANCEL_TEST && e.getTeam().getName().equalsIgnoreCase("Red")) e.setCancelled(true);
        String breaker = e.getBreaker() == null ? "the server" : e.getBreaker().getName();
        log("BedBreak team=" + e.getTeam().getName() + " by " + breaker + " cancelled=" + e.isCancelled());
        if (!e.isCancelled()) e.getTeam().getPlayers().forEach(this::showBedBar);
    }

The addon handles these events. Details of every getter are in Events.

Event Meaning GameStartEvent The game starts, teams are assigned GameEndEvent The game ends; getWinner() is null for a draw ArenaResetEvent Before (PRE) and after (POST) a map reset ArenaStateChangeEvent The arena changes state, for example WAITING to STARTING TeamsAssignedEvent Players were distributed into teams PlayerJoinArenaEvent A player joins (also a rejoin); can be cancelled PlayerLeaveArenaEvent A player leaves, with the reason (command, quit, ...) PlayerSpectateEvent A player becomes a spectator PlayerRespawnArenaEvent A player respawns PlayerKillEvent A player dies: victim, killer, final kill, cause BedBreakEvent A bed is destroyed; can be cancelled ShopPurchaseEvent A player buys a shop item; can be cancelled ShopItemStackEvent An item is built or given from the shop ArmorEquipEvent A player's armor tier changes TeamUpgradeEvent A team buys an upgrade level TrapTriggerEvent An enemy triggers a team trap PlayerSendToLobbyEvent A player is sent to the lobby PartyChangeEvent A party is created, changed or disbanded

docs.title: Registering content
docs.text: Everything is registered in one method. All register* calls take your plugin as owner; see Registering your own content for the rules.

docs.title: Phase action
docs.text:
A phase action is a name you can put in the actions of a game phase. This one tells everyone in the arena a message and logs it. See Phase actions.

        // Phase action: put "NBWLOG:hello" in a phase's actions in config.yml.
        api.registerPhaseAction(this, "NBWLOG", (arena, arg) -> {
            log("PhaseAction NBWLOG arena=" + arena.getName() + " phase=" + arena.getCurrentPhase() + " arg='" + arg + "'");
            arena.getPlayers().forEach(p -> p.sendMessage(ChatColor.AQUA + "[NBWLOG] " + arg));
        });

Try it: add NBWLOG:hello to the actions of a phase in config.yml. When the phase runs, players get [NBWLOG] hello.

docs.title: Shop item logic
docs.text:
The key you register is used as itemLogic on a shop item. Returning true consumes one item. See Shop item logic.

        // Shop logic: set "itemLogic: NBWLIGHTNING" on a shop item in items.yml.
        api.registerShopLogic(this, "NBWLIGHTNING", (player, arena) -> {
            player.getWorld().strikeLightningEffect(player.getLocation());
            log("ShopLogic NBWLIGHTNING used by " + player.getName() + " in " + arena.getName());
            return true;
        });

Try it: set itemLogic: NBWLIGHTNING on an item in items.yml, buy it and right-click: a lightning effect, and the item is used up.

docs.title: Armor tier
docs.text:
A tier is a name, a rank and the four pieces. Buying an item with onBuyEvent: GIVE_ARMOR and one of the tier's pieces gives the whole tier, and a lower-ranked tier never replaces a higher one. See Armor tiers.

        // Armor tier: a shop item with onBuyEvent GIVE_ARMOR and e.g. TURTLE_HELMET gives the whole tier.
        api.registerArmorTier(this, new ArmorTierDefinition("NBWTEST", 2, Material.DIAMOND_BOOTS,
                Material.IRON_LEGGINGS, Material.GOLDEN_CHESTPLATE, Material.TURTLE_HELMET));

Try it: a shop item with onBuyEvent: GIVE_ARMOR and TURTLE_HELMET gives diamond boots, iron leggings, a golden chestplate and a turtle helmet.

docs.title: Upgrade and trap
docs.text:
Upgrades and traps share one definition. NBWSPEED has two levels costing 2 and 4 diamonds, applies Speed to the team and is applied again after a respawn. NBWBLIND is a trap that blinds the enemy who enters the base. See Upgrades and traps.

        // Upgrade (use "upg:NBWSPEED" in the upgrade GUI file) and trap ("upg:NBWBLIND").
        api.registerUpgrade(this, UpgradeDefinition.upgrade("NBWSPEED", 2, Material.SUGAR, List.of(2, 4),
                (player, team, level) -> {
                    player.addPotionEffect(new PotionEffect(PotionEffectType.SPEED, Integer.MAX_VALUE, level - 1));
                    log("Upgrade effect NBWSPEED level " + level + " on " + player.getName());
                }).reapplyOnRespawn());
        api.registerUpgrade(this, UpgradeDefinition.trap("NBWBLIND", 1, Material.INK_SAC, List.of(1),
                (enemy, team, arena) -> {
                    enemy.addPotionEffect(new PotionEffect(PotionEffectType.BLINDNESS, 100, 0));
                    log("Trap NBWBLIND triggered on " + enemy.getName() + " at team " + team.getName());
                }));

Try it: put upg:NBWSPEED and upg:NBWBLIND in the upgrade GUI file and buy them in a game.

docs.title: Subcommand
docs.text:
registerCommand adds a subcommand of /bw. The same command can live in several contexts; here it works in a game, for admins in the lobby and from the console (the console methods are performConsole and tabCompleteConsole). It also appears in /bw help. See Subcommands.

        // One subcommand in three places: /bw nbwinfo in a game, as a lobby admin, and from the console.
        api.registerCommand(this, new InfoCommand("nbwinfo"), CommandContext.GAME, CommandContext.LOBBY_ADMIN, CommandContext.CONSOLE);

The command class implements AddonCommand: name, description, syntax, example and what to do when a player or the console runs it.

    /** Prints the arena's extra data and the team upgrade levels. */
    private final class InfoCommand implements AddonCommand {
        private final String name;

        InfoCommand(String name) {
            this.name = name;
        }

        @Override public String getName() { return name; }
        @Override public String getDescription() { return "Logger addon: shows extra data and upgrade levels"; }
        @Override public String getSyntax() { return "/bw " + name; }
        @Override public String getExample() { return "/bw " + name; }

        @Override
        public void perform(Player player, String[] args, ArenaView arena) {
            player.sendMessage("Command " + name + " works. Arena: " + (arena == null ? "none" : arena.getName()));
            if (arena != null) describe(player, arena);
        }

        @Override
        public void performConsole(CommandSender sender, String[] args) {
            if (args.length < 2) {
                sender.sendMessage("Usage: bw " + name + " <arena>");
                return;
            }
            NewBedwarsAPI.get().getArena(args[1]).ifPresentOrElse(arena -> describe(sender, arena),
                    () -> sender.sendMessage("No arena " + args[1]));
        }

        @Override
        public List<String> tabCompleteConsole(CommandSender sender, String[] args) {
            return args.length == 2 ? NewBedwarsAPI.get().getArenas().stream().map(ArenaView::getName).collect(Collectors.toList()) : List.of();
        }
    }

Try it: run /bw nbwinfo in a game, as an admin in the lobby, and bw nbwinfo <arena> in the console, where the arena name tab-completes.

docs.title: Extra data and the arena editor
docs.text:
Extra data is your own storage inside an arena or a team. It is saved in the arena file, namespaced by your plugin name, and NewBedwars never touches it. The addon counts games on the arena when a game starts and wins on the winning team. See Extra data.

    @EventHandler(priority = EventPriority.MONITOR)
    public void onStart(GameStartEvent e) {
        String teams = e.getArena().getTeams().stream()
                .map(t -> t.getName() + "=" + t.getPlayers().size()).collect(Collectors.joining(", "));
        ExtraData extra = e.getArena().getExtra(this);
        extra.set("games", extra.getInt("games", 0) + 1);
        log("GameStart " + a(e) + " teams: " + teams + " (games played with this addon: " + extra.getInt("games", 0) + ")");
    }

    @EventHandler(priority = EventPriority.MONITOR)
    public void onEnd(GameEndEvent e) {
        TeamView w = e.getWinner();
        if (w != null) {
            ExtraData extra = w.getExtra(this);
            extra.set("wins", extra.getInt("wins", 0) + 1);
        }
        log("GameEnd " + a(e) + " winner=" + (w == null ? "DRAW" : w.getName()));
    }

The values are printed by the addon's describe method, which /bw nbwinfo and /nbwlog use, and survive a restart (extra in the arena JSON).

The arena editor changes arenas that are being set up or waiting for players. /nbwlog edit creates a team, adds and removes a generator, removes the team and saves, all with the position of the player running it. It refuses while a game is running (the editor throws, and the addon reports the exception). See Editing arenas.

    private void runEditorTest(Player player) {
        NewBedwarsAPI api = NewBedwarsAPI.get();
        ArenaView arena = api.getArena(player.getWorld()).orElse(null);
        if (arena == null) {
            player.sendMessage("Stand in the arena world (setup or waiting) first.");
            return;
        }
        try {
            ArenaEditor editor = api.edit(arena);
            int generatorsBefore = arena.getGenerators().size();
            TeamEditor team = editor.createTeam("NbwTest", ChatColor.LIGHT_PURPLE);
            team.setSpawn(player.getLocation());
            team.setColor(ChatColor.AQUA);
            player.sendMessage("Created team NbwTest, teams now: " + arena.getTeams().stream().map(TeamView::getName).toList());
            editor.addGenerator(GeneratorKind.DIAMOND, player.getLocation());
            player.sendMessage("Generators " + generatorsBefore + " -> " + arena.getGenerators().size());
            player.sendMessage("removeGenerator: " + editor.removeGenerator(arena.getGenerators().size() - 1));
            player.sendMessage("removeTeam: " + editor.removeTeam("NbwTest"));
            editor.save();
            player.sendMessage("Editor OK. Teams: " + arena.getTeams().size() + ", generators: " + arena.getGenerators().size());
        } catch (RuntimeException ex) {
            player.sendMessage(ChatColor.RED + "Editor refused: " + ex);
        }
    }

docs.title: Display
docs.text: The display APIs are new in 2.8-beta. See Display for all of them.

docs.title: Placeholder
docs.text:
One registration works in tablists.yml as {logger_events}, and in scoreboards.yml and bossBars.yml as /logger_events/. See Placeholders. The counter is incremented by the addon's log method, which every handler calls.

        // Placeholder: {logger_events} in tablists.yml, /logger_events/ in scoreboards.yml and bossBars.yml.
        api.registerPlaceholder(this, "logger_events", (viewer, arena) -> String.valueOf(loggedEvents.get()));

docs.title: Boss bar
docs.text:
When a bed is broken, every player of that team gets a red, full boss bar for five seconds. The bar is shown with getBossBars().show(...) and removed by a normal Bukkit scheduler task; NewBedwars also removes it if the player leaves first. See Boss bars. The call is at the end of onBed, shown earlier.

    /** Addon boss bar: red, full, removed again after 5 seconds (NewBedwars also removes it when the player leaves). */
    private void showBedBar(Player player) {
        AddonBossBar bar = NewBedwarsAPI.get().getBossBars()
                .show(this, player, "&cYour bed is gone!", BarColor.RED, BarStyle.SOLID, 1.0);
        Bukkit.getScheduler().runTaskLater(this, bar::remove, 5 * 20L);
    }

docs.title: Scoreboard and tab list
docs.text:
Both events are fired just before a changed sidebar or tab list is sent, and only when something changed. The scoreboard listener appends a line when there are fewer than 15; the tab list listener adds to the footer. See Scoreboards and Tab list.

    /** Appends one line to the sidebar when there is room. */
    @EventHandler
    public void onScoreboard(ScoreboardUpdateEvent e) {
        List<String> lines = e.getLines();
        if (lines.size() >= ScoreboardUpdateEvent.MAX_LINES) return;
        lines.add(ChatColor.GRAY + "Logged: " + loggedEvents.get());
        e.setLines(lines);
    }

    /** Adds a line to the footer of the tab list. */
    @EventHandler
    public void onTablist(TablistUpdateEvent e) {
        String footer = e.getFooter();
        String line = ChatColor.GRAY + "Events logged: " + loggedEvents.get();
        e.setFooter(footer.isEmpty() ? line : footer + "\n" + line);
    }

Note

The values only change when NewBedwars sends a changed sidebar or tab list. The counter alone does not cause a new send, so it can lag behind until something else changes. Call ScoreboardService#refresh or TablistService#refresh if you need it to update at once.

docs.title: Reading game modes
docs.text:
api.getModes() returns the game modes of modes.yml. The methods return a CompletableFuture that completes on the server thread, so the addon sends its messages directly from the callback. /nbwlog modes lists the modes:

        if (args.length > 0 && args[0].equalsIgnoreCase("modes")) {
            api.getModes().getModes().thenAccept(modes -> modes.forEach(m -> sender.sendMessage(
                    " mode " + m.id() + " maxInTeam=" + m.maxInTeam() + " phases=" + m.gamePhases() + " builtIn=" + m.builtIn())));
            return true;
        }

docs.title: Cleaning up
docs.text:
NewBedwars removes everything registered with owner when your plugin is disabled, or when you call api.unregisterAll(plugin): the phase action, shop logic, armor tier, upgrades and traps, subcommands, placeholders and boss bars the addon showed. The addon therefore has no onDisable.

What the addon has to do itself:

  • Bukkit listeners are removed by Bukkit when the plugin is disabled, so nothing is needed there. Repeating tasks and anything you hold on to (threads, files, connections) are yours to stop.
  • Extra data stays in the arena file on purpose. Remove your keys yourself if an addon should leave no trace.
  • Keep no references to ArenaView, TeamView or Player objects after the game ended.

docs.title: Testing checklist
docs.text:
Start a test server with NewBedwars and the addon, make yourself op (or give yourself nbwlogger.use) and add the config lines from the sections above.

  1. Start the server: the console shows the API version and Registered phase action, ....
  2. Run /nbwlog: arenas, teams and your stats are printed. /nbwlog chat toggles chat output.
  3. Join an arena, leave, join again: Join and Leave lines appear (try the command and quitting the game).
  4. Wait for the start: State, TeamsAssigned and GameStart lines appear; games goes up in /nbwlog.
  5. With NBWLOG:hello in a phase, check the chat message when the phase runs.
  6. Buy items, armor and upgrades: Shop, ShopItem, ArmorEquip and Upgrade lines. Test NBWLIGHTNING, NBWTEST armor and NBWSPEED (also after dying).
  7. Let an enemy enter a base with NBWBLIND: Blindness and a Trap line.
  8. Break a bed: BedBreak, and the red boss bar for the team for five seconds.
  9. Kill players (also by void and mob): Kill lines. Spectate after the final death.
  10. Check the sidebar line Logged: N and the tab list footer Events logged: N.
  11. Run /bw nbwinfo in a game, in the lobby as admin and bw nbwinfo <arena> from the console.
  12. Finish the game: GameEnd and ArenaReset PRE and POST; wins goes up for the winner. Use /lobby to see SendToLobby.
  13. Stand in a WAITING arena and run /nbwlog edit; then run it during a game, where it must refuse.
  14. Run /nbwlog modes.
  15. Restart: the games and wins values must still be there.
  16. Disable the addon (/plugman unload NewBedwarsEventLogger): the action, item logic, upgrades, command, placeholder and bars disappear without errors, and registering works again after loading it.

The README of the example has the same list as a table of features and how to test each.

docs.title: Players
docs.text: See Getting started for how to get NewBedwarsAPI api and the dependency.

docs.title: Players: join, spectate, leave
docs.text:
Important

New in 2.8-beta.

The same paths as the commands, so parties, rejoining, events and messages work as usual. Call them on the server thread with an arena of this server (IllegalArgumentException otherwise; in network mode use requestNetworkJoin on a lobby server).

Method Does join(player, arena) like /bw join <arena>: a party leader brings the party, a player who left this arena's running game rejoins. The newbedwars.bw.join permission is not checked, so your addon decides who may join spectate(player, arena) like /bw spectate <arena>, without the newbedwars.bw.spectate permission leave(player) takes the player out of the arena they play, wait or spectate in and sends them to the lobby (during a game they can rejoin when rejoining is on); false when they are in no arena sendToLobby(player) leave for a player in an arena, otherwise a teleport to the lobby through PlayerSendToLobbyEvent (reason ADDON); false when there is no lobby or the teleport was cancelled

join and spectate return a JoinResult, and the player also gets the usual chat message:

JoinResult Meaning JOINED, REJOINED, SPECTATING done (isSuccess() is true) NOT_PARTY_LEADER, PARTY_TOO_BIG, PARTIES_NOT_ALLOWED party rules ALREADY_IN_ARENA, NOT_ENABLED, FULL the player or the arena RUNNING, ENDING, RESTARTING the game state does not allow joining (spectate a RUNNING game instead) NOT_RUNNING, SPECTATORS_DISABLED spectating only CANCELLED an addon cancelled PlayerJoinArenaEvent or PlayerSpectateEvent FAILED anything else, e.g. the rejoin place is gone or the player plays in another arena 
api.getArena("Castle").ifPresent(arena -> {
    JoinResult result = api.join(player, arena);
    if (result == JoinResult.RUNNING) api.spectate(player, arena);
});

docs.title: Parties
docs.text:
Important

New in 2.8-beta.

api.getParty(player) returns the player's PartyView (getLeader, getMembers, getOnlineMembers, contains, size). It is a live view: the getters always show the current members. In network mode the proxy keeps the parties and this is the copy it sends to the server.

PartyChangeEvent fires after a party on this server changed, with getChange(): CREATED (getPlayer() is the leader), JOINED, LEFT, KICKED, LEADER_CHANGED (getPlayer() is the new leader) and DISBANDED (getPlayer() is null, the party is empty). Changes that arrive from the proxy don't fire it.

@EventHandler
public void onParty(PartyChangeEvent e) {
    if (e.getChange() == PartyChangeEvent.Change.JOINED) {
        e.getParty().getOnlineMembers().forEach(p -> p.sendMessage("A new member joined your party"));
    }
}

docs.title: Statistics and leaderboards
Messages and languages
docs.text:
Important

New in 2.8-beta.

Players choose their language with /lang. Addons can use the same language for their own texts:

Method Returns getLanguage(player) en, pl, de, es, fr or ru getMessage(player, key) the message in the player's language: one your addon registered, or a NewBedwars message from the language files; missing translations fall back to English, unknown keys give "". & colours are translated getMessage(player, key, replacements) the same with placeholders replaced, e.g. Map.of("/player/", name) registerMessages(owner, language, messages) adds your messages for one language (calling it again replaces that language). Register en at least. Removed when your plugin is disabled 
api.registerMessages(this, "en", Map.of("MyAddon-Welcome", "&aWelcome, /player/!"));
api.registerMessages(this, "pl", Map.of("MyAddon-Welcome", "&aWitaj, /player/!"));

player.sendMessage(api.getMessage(player, "MyAddon-Welcome", Map.of("/player/", player.getName())));

Addon messages win over NewBedwars messages with the same key, so give your keys a prefix.

docs.title: Registering your own content
docs.text: See Getting started for how to get NewBedwarsAPI api and the dependency.

docs.title: Registering your own content
docs.text: All register* methods take your plugin as owner. A name that already exists throws IllegalArgumentException. Everything you register is removed automatically when your plugin is disabled (or call api.unregisterAll(plugin)).

docs.title: Phase actions
docs.text:
Usable in GamePhases in modes.yml as NAME or NAME:argument (everything after the first colon is the argument).

api.registerPhaseAction(this, "ANNOUNCE", (arena, arg) ->
        arena.getPlayers().forEach(p -> p.sendMessage(arg)));
// config.yml: - "ANNOUNCE:Diamonds are now level 2!"

docs.title: Shop item logic
docs.text:
What a special item does on right-click. Use the key as itemLogic in items.yml. Return true to consume one item.

api.registerShopLogic(this, "LIGHTNING", (player, arena) -> {
    player.getWorld().strikeLightning(player.getTargetBlock(null, 40).getLocation());
    return true;
});

(2.8-beta) When one logic serves several items, override perform(player, arena, itemName) to know which items.yml entry was used (the lambda form above only implements the two-argument method):

api.registerShopLogic(this, "SPELL", new ShopLogic() {
    @Override
    public boolean perform(Player player, ArenaView arena) {
        return false;
    }

    @Override
    public boolean perform(Player player, ArenaView arena, String itemName) {
        return castSpell(player, itemName);
    }
});

docs.title: Shop items
docs.text:
registerShopItem writes an item into items.yml when no item with that name exists yet, so server owners do not have to add it by hand. An existing item is never changed (the owner may have edited it) and stays when your addon is disabled. Register the item logic first, call it on the server thread (e.g. in onEnable), and note that the item still has to be put into a shop GUI (the panel or a GUI file) to be sold. It returns true when the item was added and throws IllegalArgumentException for invalid values (same rules as ShopEditor#saveItem). (2.7-beta)

api.registerShopLogic(this, "EMERALD_GOLEM", (player, arena) -> { /* spawn it */ return true; });
api.registerShopItem(this,
        ShopItem.of("EmeraldGolemEgg", "SNOWBALL", 1, 24, "IRON", "EMERALD_GOLEM"),
        Map.of("en", new ItemTexts("&fEmerald Golem", "&7Spawns a emerald golem;&7for /price/", ""),
               "pl", new ItemTexts("&fSmaragdowy golem", "", "")));

ShopItem.of(name, material, amount, price, priceType, logic) covers the common case; use the full ShopItem constructor for permanent items, enchantments, flags or another onBuy action. The texts are optional (without them the item is named after its name). From 2.8-beta the full constructor also takes commands, openGui, givePermission and priceMaterial for the COMMANDS, OPEN_GUI and GIVE_PERM actions and priceType OTHER (see Commands, menus and permissions); the 12-argument constructor is kept and leaves them empty.

docs.title: Armor tiers
docs.text:
A shop item with onBuyEvent: GIVE_ARMOR and a piece of the tier gives the buyer the whole tier; higher rank replaces lower. Built-in ranks: leather 0, gold 1, chainmail 2, iron 3, diamond 4, netherite 5.

api.registerArmorTier(this, new ArmorTierDefinition("COPPER", 1,
        Material.COPPER_INGOT /* boots, leggings, chestplate, helmet materials */, ...));

docs.title: Upgrades and traps
docs.text:
Use in the upgrade GUI files as upg:<name>; its prices are added to data/upgrades.yml on the first registration and are changed there (or in the panel) afterwards. Read the level with TeamView#getUpgradeLevel.

api.registerUpgrade(this, UpgradeDefinition.upgrade("SPEED", 2, Material.SUGAR, List.of(4, 8),
        (player, team, level) -> player.addPotionEffect(
                new PotionEffect(PotionEffectType.SPEED, Integer.MAX_VALUE, level - 1)))
        .reapplyOnRespawn());

api.registerUpgrade(this, UpgradeDefinition.trap("BLIND", 1, Material.INK_SAC, List.of(2),
        (enemy, team, arena) -> enemy.addPotionEffect(new PotionEffect(PotionEffectType.BLINDNESS, 100, 0))));

docs.title: Subcommands
docs.text:
Adds /bw <name>, listed in /bw help. CommandContext says where it is available: LOBBY, LOBBY_ADMIN, GAME, GAME_ADMIN, SETUP_BASIC, SETUP_NORMAL, SETUP_ADVANCED, SETUP_AUTOMATIC (SETUP_BUILDING is a deprecated alias for it) and CONSOLE (2.7-beta).

Implement AddonCommand (getName, getDescription, getSyntax, getExample, perform(player, args, arena), optional tabComplete) and register it:

api.registerCommand(this, new MyCommand(), CommandContext.GAME);

Several contexts (2.7-beta). Register the same command for every place it should work. arena in perform is the player's arena, or null outside arenas:

api.registerCommand(this, new TrimCommand(), CommandContext.LOBBY, CommandContext.GAME, CommandContext.CONSOLE);

CONSOLE makes /bw <name> work in the server console (and command blocks). It calls performConsole(sender, args) and tabCompleteConsole(sender, args) instead of the player methods. Both do nothing by default, so override them when you register for CONSOLE. Typing bw alone in the console lists the console commands.

Permission (2.8-beta). A command registered in an admin or setup context (LOBBY_ADMIN, GAME_ADMIN, SETUP_*) is usable and visible by default only to admins (newbedwars.bw.admin or op) and, for setup contexts, to the player setting up the arena. Override permission() to require your own permission instead (admins can always use it): @Override public String permission() { return "myaddon.trim"; }.

Names: two different commands may not share a name in the same place. Lobby and lobby admin count as one place, so do game and game admin, all setup modes together, and the console. The same name is allowed in places that never apply at the same time (e.g. one addon's trim in LOBBY and another's in GAME). A clash throws IllegalArgumentException.

docs.title: Shop editor and game modes
docs.text: See Getting started for how to get NewBedwarsAPI api and the dependency.

docs.title: Shop editor
docs.text:
api.getShop() returns ShopEditor, the data behind the web panel's shop editor. Every method can be called from any thread and returns a CompletableFuture; the work runs on the server thread. Changes apply at once (players see them the next time they open a shop) and the previous file is kept in data/backups/shop/.

Method Does getItems() / getItem(name) ShopItems of items.yml (items that could not be loaded on this server are left out) saveItem(item) creates the item when the name is new, changes it otherwise deleteItem(name) refused with IN_USE while a GUI or config.yml uses it getItemTexts(name) / saveItemTexts(name, texts) ItemTexts (name, shop icon description, lore) per language code getGuis() / getGui(id) ShopGuis with slots, categories, unresolved references (problems) and usedBy createGui(gui) / saveGui(gui) / deleteGui(id) deleteGui is refused while an arena or config.yml uses it getArenaShops() / setArenaShops(arena, shopGui, upgradeGui) which GUIs each arena opens; only while the arena is waiting (BUSY otherwise) getUpgradePrices() / saveUpgradePrices(upgrade, tiers) UpgradePrices of data/upgrades.yml (name, tiers, maxLevel, builtIn); a tier (UpgradeTier) is a price and a currency getOptions() materials, enchantments, flags, logic keys, upgrades, price types, buy actions and languages of this server

ShopGui.itemPrices() (2.8-beta) is a map of shop item id to ItemPrice (price, currency, amount; the last two may be null = the item's own), the ItemPrices section of the file (see Shop and upgrades). When saving, null keeps the current prices and an empty map removes them. The older ShopGui constructors still work.

Changes return a ShopResult (OK, NOT_FOUND, INVALID with the field in detail, IN_USE with the places in detail, BUSY, NAME_TAKEN, FAILED).

Warning

ShopGui.closeOnTransaction is deprecated and will be removed in the first stable release (3.0.0). The CloseOnTransaction setting of GUI files never had an effect (shops always stay open after a purchase), so it was removed from GUI files and the web panel in 2.8-beta. The record component is still there so existing addons keep compiling, but it is always false and ignored when saving. Pass false and don't read it.

ShopEditor shop = api.getShop();
shop.getItem("Wool").thenAccept(item -> item.ifPresent(wool ->
        shop.saveItem(new ShopItem(wool.name(), wool.material(), 32, wool.price(), wool.priceType(), wool.onBuy(),
                wool.logic(), wool.permanent(), wool.permission(), wool.enchantments(), wool.flags(), List.of()))));

docs.title: Game modes
docs.text:
New in 2.8-beta.

api.getModes() returns ModeService, the data behind the web panel's Modes page and its Apply mode picker. Every method can be called from any thread and returns a CompletableFuture; the work runs on the server thread and the futures complete there.

Method Does getModes() ModeInfos in the order of modes.yml, then built-in modes the file doesn't list: id, generators, gamePhases, shopGui, upgradeGui (null = the mode leaves it unchanged), maxInTeam (0 = unchanged), teams (a hint, never applied; 0 = not set), builtIn and tablist (tab list layout id, null = unchanged; saveMode rejects an unknown layout with unknown tablist: X; the old eight-argument ModeInfo constructor still exists and sets it to null) getPhaseLists() PhaseListInfos: the id and its phases (PhaseInfo: name, duration in seconds until the next phase, 0 for the last one, and actions as written in modes.yml, e.g. DIAMOND_GENERATOR:2) getArenaModes() ArenaModeInfo per arena, sorted by name: arena, waiting (only then can a mode be applied), generators, gamePhases, shopGui, upgradeGui (null when not set), maxInTeam and teams (team count) getGeneratorConfigs() ids of every loaded generator config, sorted applyMode(arena, mode) copies the mode into the arena once, like /bw setMode (generator config, phase list, GUIs and team size, each only when the mode sets it) and saves the arena. The mode name is matched ignoring case. Later edits to the mode don't change the arena

applyMode needs the arena to be waiting for players. It returns a ModeResult with a code: OK, NOT_FOUND (no such arena or mode), MISSING_PARTS (the mode names generator configs, phase lists or GUIs that don't exist; they are in missing and nothing was changed) or BUSY (a game is starting or running). With OK, teamsDiffer is true when the arena's team count differs from the mode's teams.

docs.title: Editing modes, phase lists and generator configs
docs.text:
The edit methods return an EditResult with a code, problems (short English reasons) and usedBy. File work runs off the main thread; the futures still complete on the server thread, after the change was written and loaded. Edits never change arenas: an arena keeps the settings and the generator config object it already has until you apply a mode again.

Method Does saveMode(ModeInfo) creates a mode or replaces the one with the same id (ignoring case, the existing spelling is kept); builtIn is ignored. Only that block of modes.yml is rewritten, comments elsewhere stay. The id must match [A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,32}; generators, gamePhases, shopGui and upgradeGui must be null/blank (unchanged) or exist; maxInTeam and teams must be 0 to 100 deleteMode(id) removes a mode. Built-in modes (Solo, Doubles, Squads, Rush, Duels) can be edited but not deleted savePhaseList(PhaseListInfo) creates or replaces a phase list: at least one phase, named, duration of 0 or more, every action registered (DIAMOND_GENERATOR and EMERALD_GENERATOR need a level) deletePhaseList(id) removes a phase list; refused while a mode or an arena uses it, and for the lists that ship with NewBedwars getGeneratorConfigFiles() GeneratorConfigInfo (id, fileName, builtIn) for every file in generators/, sorted by id getGeneratorConfigText(id) the raw YAML of that config, or null when there is none saveGeneratorConfig(id, yaml) creates generators/<id>.yml or replaces the file of that id, then reloads the generator configs. The text must be YAML of at most 64 KB, its ConfigurationId must equal id and it must load as a valid generator config deleteGeneratorConfig(id) deletes the file and reloads; refused while a mode or an arena uses it, and for the bundled configs

EditResult.code is OK, NOT_FOUND, INVALID (see problems; nothing was changed), IN_USE (see usedBy, e.g. mode Squads or arena castle), BUILT_IN (a delete of something that ships with NewBedwars) or FAILED (the file could not be written; problems holds the error).

ArenaView.getGeneratorConfig() and getGamePhases() return the ids of the generator config and the phase list an arena uses (null when it has none).

ModeService modes = api.getModes();
modes.applyMode("Island", "Duels").thenAccept(result -> {
    if (result.code() == ModeResult.Code.OK && result.teamsDiffer()) {
        getLogger().warning("Island has a different team count than Duels");
    }
});
